## LLM-agent workflow reports new proofs on positivity problems in algebraic combinatorics
2026-11-25 · mathematics · University of Washington; Pacific Northwest National Laboratory
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-patternminer-schubert-positivity.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33966

A preprint describes PatternMiner, in which an LLM agent generates mathematical datasets, trains small models (MLPs, small transformers, trees), interprets them and formulates conjectures that are tested against counterexamples in mathematical software, applied to five positivity problems from Stanley's survey. The paper gives proofs, labelled LLM-generated, that for every n>=5 no fixed number of retained flag dimensions suffices for projection tests of Schubert structure-constant vanishing, an equivariant positivity inequality that proves Conjectures A and B of Chen et al. on equivariant nonvanishing, a character-row evaluation formula, a restricted case of Kazhdan-Lusztig combinatorial invariance, and Schur positivity for a family of immanant coefficients, supported by finite checks such as 776,891 coefficients over 1,587 shape instances. Proofs received an internal adversarial review only; no proof-kernel or independent mathematician check is reported, one decisive construction needed human redirection, and the comparison with direct LLM attempts is not compute-matched.

## Deep learning predicts DNA damage response protein levels from routine slides
2026-11-25 · medicine · Johns Hopkins University; Johns Hopkins School of Medicine
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-he-histopathology-ddr-protein-prediction.html
Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.11.17.766760v1.full

Gated attention-based multiple-instance learning on frozen pathology foundation-model tile embeddings predicted reverse-phase protein array pathway scores from 1,673 TCGA haematoxylin-and-eosin whole-slide images covering 1,527 patients with breast, endometrial, cervical and ovarian cancer and uterine carcinosarcoma. For the 11-protein DNA damage composite the out-of-fold Spearman correlation was 0.43 against 0.31 for a cancer-type-mean baseline, about 0.29-0.30 within cancer type, and at most 0.00 with shuffled targets. Cross-validation was cancer-type-stratified and site-grouped. This is a moderate retrospective association in one public cohort: there is no external validation, no clinical or treatment-response outcome, and the authors list separating the signal from proliferation as future work, noting the cell-cycle score was predicted more strongly.

## Machine learning forecasts acute food crises and separates predictive from causal drivers
2026-11-25 · multidisciplinary · European Commission, Joint Research Centre; University of Valencia; Integrated Food Security Phase Classification Global Support Unit
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-causal-ml-acute-food-crises-drivers.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34629

Missing-data-resilient machine-learning pipelines, including gradient boosting and a tabular foundation model, forecast acute food crisis occurrence 3, 6 and 9 months ahead across 80 countries using monthly subnational data for 2007-2024, exceeding no-skill baselines by 15 to 50 percentage points in PR-AUC under nested cross-validation. TreeSHAP profiles fell into three recurring archetypes. Doubly robust causal estimates indicated that acute conflict events, which carried the weakest predictive signal, are primary causal drivers, while agroclimatology was the only dimension where predictive and causal importance agreed. The authors report that skill tracks crisis prevalence, that the causal effects are modest and only moderately robust to unmeasured confounding, and that they depend on an assumed causal graph; several variables were reported as non-identifiable. The work is a preprint.

## Interpretable machine learning maps wastewater treatment conditions
2026-11-24 · chemistry · Xinjiang Institute of Technology; Lanzhou University; Lanzhou Jiaotong University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-xgboost-pva-treatment-associations.html
Source: https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11299105/v1

An XGBoost model fitted to 1,423 experimental and literature-derived samples linked iron/carbon ratio and operating conditions to chemical oxygen demand removal in polyvinyl-alcohol wastewater treatment. SHAP analysis identified iron/carbon ratio as the strongest modeled factor and a pH-dependent interaction window. Reported test R² was 0.8045, but the paper selected its final model using that test set, limiting an unbiased generalization claim. The preprint offers model-derived process associations, not a confirmed causal mechanism or validated industrial-scale control policy.

## Satellite machine learning measures inundation across 542,850 conserved wetland sites
2026-11-24 · climate · University of Nebraska-Lincoln
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-svm-inundation-conserved-wetland-lands.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-82320-0

A Support Vector Machine classifier applied to Sentinel-2 and Dynamic World data in Google Earth Engine mapped surface-water inundation across 542,850 wetland-related Conservation Reserve Program and Wetlands Reserve Program sites from 2018 to 2024. Measurable inundation occurred on 44.20% of CRP and 76.62% of WRP lands, persisted longer on WRP and on longer-enrolled CRP lands, and tracked hydric soil distribution. Reported validation accuracy was 95.50% on a random 75/25 split of 50,000 labelled points (RF 96.18%), but samples were split at point level so spatial autocorrelation may inflate it, there was no field hydrological validation, and surface water alone does not show conservation benefit.

## Learned lesion-network models identify shared and specific stroke cognition patterns
2026-11-24 · medicine · University Medical Center Utrecht; Meta VCI Map consortium; Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf; Research Centre Jülich
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-stroke-lesion-networks-cognitive-impairment.html
Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.11.10.765579v1

A November 24, 2026 preprint analyzed 3,034 patients across 13 stroke cohorts using learned models of lesion anatomy, network connectivity and clinical characteristics. Structural lesion connectivity supplied most of the gain beyond clinical information and infarct size, with left anterior thalamic connectivity consistently informative across cognitive outcomes. Benefits persisted for several outcomes when entire cohorts were held out. The results support a bounded lesion-in-context account of cognitive impairment, without establishing causal circuitry or clinical readiness.

## Machine learning selects an exploratory senescence-related gene score in PMOS
2026-11-24 · medicine · Seventh People's Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Changhai Hospital, Naval Medical University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-sasp-gene-score-pmos.html
Source: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fendo.2026.1929626/full

Using two public ovarian-cell datasets (13 PMOS and 9 control samples), univariate logistic regression, SVM-RFE and LASSO selected a five-gene SASP-related score (DYNLRB2, MMP9, A1BG, PGD, APLP2) with apparent AUC 0.991 on the development data and AUC 0.838 in an exploratory skeletal-muscle dataset (10 versus 13 samples). The authors state the apparent AUC should not be interpreted as evidence of diagnostic ability: dataset origin is confounded with cell type, the muscle dataset is not tissue-matched, no individual gene there remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and virtual screening against MMP9 is unvalidated. No laboratory experiments were reported.

## OpenAI model claims the matrix multiplication exponent is 9/4
2026-11-24 · computer science · OpenAI
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-openai-math-matrix-multiplication.html
Source: https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/history.md

OpenAI added to its openai/math repository manuscripts produced by an unnamed internal model claiming that the exponent of square matrix multiplication is exactly 9/4 over every field, with a lower bound of n^(9/4)/2 multiplication or division gates. The same release claims separations of Valiant's classes VF, VBP, VP and VNP (subsuming a VP ≠ VNP manuscript added on 23 November), circuit lower bounds for the permanent, the Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture with an exponential bound, a strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programming (Smale's ninth problem) and a disproof of the polynomial Hirsch conjecture. The abstract describes the 9/4 upper bound as known; this record does not assess that statement against published bounds. No referee or independent review is reported.

## Survival learning prioritizes cohort-specific NFKB1 associations in colorectal cancer
2026-11-24 · medicine · Fujian Medical University Union Hospital
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-nfkb1-colorectal-prognostic-associations.html
Source: https://www.wjgnet.com/2218-4333/full/v17/i11/125917.htm

A study used penalized Cox models and CoxBoost to prioritize NFKB1 for retrospective colorectal-cancer survival analysis. Higher expression was associated with favorable survival in selected external cohorts, but the adjusted association was not significant in TCGA-COAD. Model discrimination was modest: the best overall mean time-dependent AUC was 0.650. A separate spatial analysis used one tissue specimen and does not establish macrophage-specific causality. NFKB1 remains an exploratory association, without a validated clinical cutoff or demonstrated treatment benefit.

## Multimodal machine learning prioritizes candidate inhibitors of giant cancer cells
2026-11-24 · biology · UPMC Hillman Cancer Center, University of Pittsburgh; Carnegie Mellon University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-multimodal-screen-polyploid-giant-cancer-cell-inhibitors.html
Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.11.22.767421v1.full

A multimodal ensemble combining chemical fingerprints, drug-induced cell morphology, transcriptomic perturbation profiles and biological annotations was trained on screening data from four breast cancer cell lines, reaching mean Pearson correlation 0.403 and recovering 27.9% of experimentally identified hits in held-out screening data. The model ranked 21,367 compounds from an external library for testing; six candidates preferentially suppressed polyploid giant cancer cells in at least three paclitaxel-treated cell lines, and AZD-8055 and voxtalisib reduced their abundance by at least 70% in all four. Evidence is limited to cell lines and modest predictive accuracy, selectivity against normal cells was not read, and the preprint is not peer reviewed.

## Machine learning prioritises osteoarthritis genes tested under macrophage stretch
2026-11-24 · medicine · Shuguang Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Shanghai Academy of Traditional Chinese Medicine
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-ml-osteoarthritis-macrophage-stretch-genes.html
Source: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1944015/full

Random forest ranking and LASSO regression narrowed a 168-gene synovial co-expression module to five candidates (E2F3, C6orf211, NDUFC2, SPCS2, DOCK10) using public datasets (discovery 29 normal and 30 osteoarthritis samples; auxiliary GSE89408 with 28 and 22). The combined score reached AUC 0.817 in discovery and 0.797 in the auxiliary cohort. In LPS-activated RAW264.7 macrophages (six biological replicates per group), cyclic stretch lowered E2F3, SPCS2 and DOCK10 and raised NDUFC2 relative to LPS alone, alongside lower inflammatory readouts. The authors note the auxiliary cohort also informed selection and is not independent validation, the sample is small, the cell line is murine, there was no stretch-only or time-course control, and the LPS-induced E2F3 protein increase was not significant.

## Machine learning links multidomain profiles to fall history
2026-11-24 · medicine · Shahid Bahonar University of Kerman; University of Saskatchewan; Sport Science Research Institute
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-ml-fall-history-profiles.html
Source: https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11438391/v1

In a cross-sectional study of 147 community-dwelling adults aged 55 and older, machine-learning models classified ordered past-year fall-history groups from physical-function, activity, health and social measures. Random Forest reported four-class accuracy of 0.946 and binary AUC of 0.968 under internal five-fold validation after excluding fall-location, fall-situation and fear-of-falling variables. The preprint describes associations with recorded fall history, not prediction of future falls. A small, imbalanced single-region sample and self-reported measures limit generalization; external and prospective validation remain necessary.

## Machine learning derives an exploratory two-gene signature in gastric cancer
2026-11-24 · medicine · China-Japan Union Hospital of Jilin University, Jilin University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-hsp-gene-signature-gastric-cancer.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12935-026-04515-9

Differential expression and summary-data-based Mendelian randomization on TCGA gastric cancer data prioritized 24 heat-shock-protein-associated genes, consensus clustering defined two molecular clusters, and LASSO-Cox regression derived an exploratory F7-PRNP prognostic signature. siRNA knockdown of F7 or PRNP inhibited proliferation, migration and invasion in HGC27 and AGS cells. The authors state that derivation and evaluation used the same TCGA cohort, so the performance estimates are likely optimistic and independent validation is required; compound prioritization, docking and molecular dynamics are computational only.

## GPT-6.2 protein designs show binding across five targets in laboratory tests
2026-11-24 · biology · OpenAI; Onava
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-gpt6-protein-binder-lab-tests.html
Source: https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-models-demonstrate-intrinsic-protein-design-capabilities/

OpenAI reports that Onava laboratory tests found binding for 35 of 322 minibinders based on GPT-6.2-designed structures, with at least one hit for each of five targets. GPT-6.2 generated backbone designs using reasoning and general-purpose code, while SolubleMPNN supplied sequences and specialized models helped select candidates. The November 24, 2026 announcement links a preprint; the findings do not establish an end-to-end workflow without specialized models, independent replication, specificity, therapeutic activity or clinical benefit.

## Generative models guide ribozymes that retain activity at high temperature
2026-11-24 · biology · Sorbonne Université; CNRS; ESPCI Paris; Institut Polytechnique de Paris; Sapienza University of Rome
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-generative-ribozyme-thermal-activity.html
Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.11.21.768297v1

A November 24, 2026 preprint reports laboratory-tested catalytic RNA designs that remain active at 60°C. A learned evolutionary sequence model combined with an independent RNA thermodynamic score generated variants that preserved function more often than either score alone. Across 2,500 designed variants from ten starting sequences, the jointly favored group had a 72.5% high-temperature activity hit rate, compared with 7.8% for the evolutionary-score group and 0.4% for the physical-score group. The result is limited to one ribozyme family and the study’s assay.

## Generative AI designs Type I photosensitizers tested in cells and mice
2026-11-24 · chemistry · Hunan University; Hengyang Normal University; Second Xiangya Hospital, Central South University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-generative-ai-type-i-photosensitizer-design.html
Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13795365/

A cross-attention classifier trained on 1,338 curated photosensitizers (85.8% accuracy and ROC-AUC 0.918 on a scaffold split) and an RNN scaffold-decorating generator proposed candidates on a redesigned tetracyclic scaffold. Six were synthesised and all produced superoxide under light. The lead compound had IC50 3.3 micromolar in 4T1 cells under normoxia and 4.5 micromolar at 2% oxygen, with similar values in HepG2 and MCF-7, and markedly slowed 4T1 tumour growth in mice over 14 days with four animals per group. Validation covers one scaffold and six molecules, the lead was also phototoxic to normal HUVEC cells (IC50 3.5 micromolar under normoxia), hypoxia attenuated but did not abolish its effect, and the in vivo group size was small.

## Deep learning EEG metric linked to mortality in obstructive sleep apnea
2026-11-24 · medicine · Seoul National University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-eeg-respiratory-gap-sleep-apnea-mortality.html
Source: https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.11.22.26368628v1.full

A deep-learning model trained on 22,044 polysomnography recordings estimated the apnea-hypopnea index from a single EEG channel, correlating r=0.88 with the scored index in internal testing and r=0.50 to 0.62 in three external test sets. Two derived metrics, the discrepancy between the EEG-based and scored index and an estimate from epochs without scored respiratory events, were associated with all-cause and non-cardiovascular mortality among participants free of cardiovascular disease after adjustment for the apnea-hypopnea index and clinical risk factors; the event-free estimate was also associated with cardiovascular mortality in the highest versus lowest quartile. Data came from the KISS, MESA, MrOS and SHHS cohorts. The findings are retrospective associations in a preprint, external agreement is weaker, hazard ratios and per-cohort sizes were not reviewed, and the authors suggest the discrepancy is not solely model error.

## AI-designed visual stimuli probe how perceptual learning changes decisions
2026-11-24 · biology · McGill University; Université de Montréal; Mila
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-dorsalnet-perceptual-learning-readout.html
Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.11.23.768712v1

A November 24, 2026 preprint used the learned DorsalNet visual model to design motion stimuli targeting different model stages, then tested training in 19 human observers. After three days, ten observers trained on late-stage stimuli showed increased perceptual sensitivity, while nine trained on early-stage stimuli mainly changed response bias. Transfer tests and model comparisons were consistent with a late-stage readout account. Cortical stages were not directly recorded, and separate participant groups limit causal comparison.

## Deep learning scores Claudin18.2 staining in gastric cancer slides across clones
2026-11-24 · medicine · Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center; Sun Yat-sen University School of Computer Science and Engineering; Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-claudin182-ihc-deep-learning-gastric.html
Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13794020/

A pipeline that scores Claudin18.2 immunohistochemistry on whole-slide images used a LoRA-adapted UNI pathology foundation model for tumour recognition, adapter-based staining-intensity classification and two rounds of active learning. Agreement with pathologist-consensus 2/3+ scoring was ICC 0.849 on 195 internal test slides and 0.894 on 135 prospectively collected slides, and ICC 0.792-0.827 for three other antibody clones tested without retraining. In a non-randomised reader study, AI assistance improved every pathologist's agreement with the reference standard and shortened review time. The authors state the study is single-centre with limited prospective and cross-clone cohorts, uses expert consensus rather than absolute ground truth, may propagate errors across modules, and provides no treatment-response or outcome data; at the 50% cutoff the retrospective AUC was lower than one pathologist's.

## Epigenetic deep learning detects a lifestyle-trial signature
2026-11-24 · biology · Tally Health; University of California, San Diego; TruDiagnostic
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-cheekai-lifestyle-intervention-signature.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.21.768329

CheekAI neural networks trained on 25,400 buccal methylation profiles from 14,716 adults were applied retrospectively to external datasets. In an existing eight-week randomized lifestyle trial with 18 intervention and 20 control participants, the model’s age-adjusted score decreased by 1.34 model-years relative to controls (p = 0.021), largely through dietary and metabolic proxy components. This preprint reports a learned methylation-score response, not demonstrated reversal of biological aging or improved health. The score was designed to reflect lifestyle proxies; a separate semaglutide analysis did not significantly reduce the overall score and showed tissue-transfer limitations.

## Learned cell-shape signatures predict confined transit
2026-11-24 · biology · Laboratoire de Physique de l’École Normale Supérieure, ENS, Université PSL, CNRS, Sorbonne Université, Université Paris Cité; Laboratoire Jean Perrin, Sorbonne Université, CNRS
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-cell-shape-confined-transit.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32990

Support-vector and logistic classifiers linked cell area and circularity to whether MDA-MB-231 breast-cancer cells would traverse microfluidic constrictions. Less circular cells were more likely to transit, and trajectory features about 30 minutes before an event were most informative. Models transferred without retraining to narrower constrictions and more adhesive surfaces. This preprint reports a condition-dependent association in one cell line, not a causal mechanism or a predictor of metastasis in patients.

## Learned brain-activity profiles guide tested drug leads in zebrafish models
2026-11-24 · biology · Sun Yat-sen University; Guangdong Pharmaceutical University; East China Normal University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-brain-profile-zebrafish-drug-leads.html
Source: https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11797074/v1

A November 24, 2026 preprint combined large-scale zebrafish brain imaging, learned clustering and random-forest ranking to select drug conditions for follow-up. Several candidates improved movement in larval toxin models and preserved dopamine-neuron reporter signals under some conditions. These are preliminary, compound- and model-dependent findings rather than evidence of Parkinson’s disease treatment in people. Some screened conditions were toxic, and retained fluorescence does not by itself establish prevention of neuronal death.

## Bivexia selects an interaction-selective LAG-3 inhibitor tested in mouse models
2026-11-24 · chemistry · Columbia University Irving Medical Center
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-bivexia-selective-lag3-inhibitor.html
Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.11.23.768516v1

A November 24, 2026 bioRxiv preprint reports that Bivexia used random-forest predictions of four protein-interaction assays to select BVX-01, a small molecule that disrupted LAG-3 interactions with tau and amyloid-beta while preserving two other tested interactions. The authors report nanomolar LAG-3 binding, activity in donor-derived neurons, and reduced pathology readouts in two mouse models, with two cohorts per model. This is preclinical evidence from the discovery study, not peer-reviewed or independent confirmation or evidence of clinical benefit; the full cascade rests on one compound, and broader target campaigns stopped at primary screening.

## Unsupervised program learning links a beta-cell signature to insulin secretion
2026-11-24 · medicine · Jinggangshan University; The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Shenzhen University of Advanced Technology; Shenzhen People’s Hospital
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-beta-cell-program-insulin-secretion.html
Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.11.23.768764v1

A November 24, 2026 preprint used donor-resolved non-negative matrix factorization and consensus program discovery to identify a beta-cell gene program reduced in type 2 diabetes. Learned program definitions were fixed before testing in other datasets. Higher program scores were associated with greater stimulated insulin release in donor-matched measurements from two laboratories. The laboratories shared most donors, so these are complementary measurements rather than independent biological replications, and the association does not establish a causal mechanism or treatment target.

## Learned receptor networks guide an experimentally tested AT1R modulator
2026-11-24 · biology · City of Hope; McGill University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-bayesian-network-at1r-modulator.html
Source: https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11606425/v1

A November 24, 2026 preprint reports that learned Bayesian networks of receptor dynamics helped prioritize an intracellular region of the angiotensin II type 1 receptor for compound screening. Laboratory signaling, radioligand and mutational tests supported a proposed negative allosteric effect of the resulting low-affinity fragment Q2. The experiments establish a bounded cellular pharmacology finding; they do not directly resolve the fragment’s binding pose or demonstrate therapeutic efficacy.

## AI-segmented imaging localizes pigmentation bias in oximetry
2026-11-24 · medicine · University Hospital Erlangen; Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg; iThera Medical GmbH; Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-ai-segmented-oximetry-pigmentation.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.22.26368599

A pretrained convolutional network separated tissue compartments in an optoacoustic imaging study of 46 healthy volunteers spanning six Fitzpatrick skin types. Across 3,016 scans and 41 wavelengths, superficial skin signals showed stronger pigmentation associations and unreliable oxygenation responses, while deeper muscle signals responded more clearly to physiological challenges. This preprint characterizes tissue- and wavelength-dependent optoacoustic measurements; it does not directly quantify pulse-oximeter error, validate oxygen saturation against an independent reference or demonstrate clinical benefit.

## Action-trained models reveal a hand–tool representational link in macaque cortex
2026-11-24 · biology · KU Leuven; VIB; NeuroSpin; University of Trento; Massachusetts General Hospital
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-action-model-macaque-hand-tool-geometry.html
Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.11.24.768489v1

A November 24, 2026 preprint compared learned visual representations with macaque brain responses to static images. A Video Swin Transformer trained on fine-grained hand–object interactions matched parietal and prefrontal hand–tool geometry better than static-object and general-action models. Functional ultrasound in two other monkeys independently supported spatial alignment of tool and human-hand responses. The findings concern representational similarity; they do not establish that interaction experience caused the cortical organization or that monkeys understand tool functions.

## Multimodal AI finds lung-cancer tissue signatures associated with survival
2026-11-23 · medicine · EPFL; University Hospital Zurich; University of Zurich; University of Bern
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-virtues-m2-lung-cancer-risk-signatures.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31451

A November 23, 2026 preprint reports that VirTues-M2 learned joint tissue morphology and spatial-protein representations to discover survival-associated cellular signatures in lung cancer. Signatures selected on 737 patients stratified survival in 316 held-out patients and transferred without retraining to a separate 39-patient cohort. Low-risk signatures marked organized immune-rich neighborhoods; high-risk signatures marked more disorganized tumor-rich tissue. These are retrospective prognostic associations with small external validation and no demonstrated treatment benefit.

## Video gait features and clinical models estimate lung function in a small cohort
2026-11-23 · medicine · Ondokuz Mayıs University; Samsun University; Duke University School of Medicine; University of Massachusetts Amherst
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-video-gait-spirometry-estimation.html
Source: https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11706261/v1

A preprint used MediaPipe Pose to extract walking features and compared 13 regressors in 100 participants (33 classified with COPD). Five repeated 90/10 internal splits gave FEV1/FVC correlation 0.701±0.135 with gradient boosting and mid-expiratory-flow correlation 0.730±0.078 with histogram boosting; linear or regularized models were strongest for several volume targets. Test sets contained about 10 people and selecting models on the same splits can inflate performance. The study did not establish an incremental benefit from video features, external validity, replacement of spirometry or clinical benefit.

## Unsupervised clustering splits Ethiopian rainfall into ten seasonal regimes
2026-11-23 · climate · Addis Ababa University; Ethiopian Meteorological Institute; Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-unsupervised-rainy-season-regimes-ethiopia.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-11586774/v1

Ward hierarchical and K-means clustering of 1981-2022 monthly rainfall, temperature and elevation from the Ethiopian Meteorological Institute's 4 km merged gridded data (more than 66,000 points) grouped Ethiopia into ten rainy-season regimes, with the number of clusters chosen by the elbow method, and the regimes were converted into a dry, short-rainy and main-rainy seasonal timetable. Agreement between the two clustering methods was checked monthly with the Adjusted Rand Index. Earlier station-based studies proposed five to eight zones; this preprint reports no validation against independent station records or forecasts, so the regimes are descriptive and not yet shown to improve forecasting or planning.

## TyG-BMI adds modest discrimination in retrospective cardiovascular prediction
2026-11-23 · medicine · Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine; Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Heilongjiang University of Chinese Medicine; Shanxi University of Chinese Medicine
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-tyg-bmi-hypertension-cvd-prediction.html
Source: https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11455132/v1

In 3,092 hypertensive CHARLS participants followed for a median eight years, a preprint compared learned cardiovascular-event predictors using baseline risk factors. Adding TyG-BMI increased reported AUC from 0.593 to 0.636; logistic regression performed best, with tree-based learners adding no advantage. This is retrospective modeling of recorded follow-up outcomes, not a prospective evaluation of a frozen model. Modest discrimination, self-reported outcomes and unresolved clinical utility limit application; the conventional epidemiological association is not itself a new AI-discovered mechanism.

## Computer vision measures diverse tomato pollen responses to heat
2026-11-23 · biology · University of Arizona; Ohio State University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-tomato-pollen-heat-response-phenotyping.html
Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.11.19.767983v1

A preprint fine-tuned CenterNet HourGlass104 to count and track pollen in approximately 300,000 time-lapse images from 218 tomato accessions and wild relatives. In vitro, raising temperature from 26°C to 34°C increased mean bursting at two hours from 14.9% to 83.1%, while tube-length responses varied: 72% of accessions had shorter tubes and 28% had equal or greater length. Manual-count agreement supported image measurements. These are controlled pollen-assay phenotypes, not demonstrated field fertility or yield benefits; genotype effects and assay generalization need further testing.

## Learned MRI models link cord motion and compression level to myelopathy severity
2026-11-23 · medicine · Balgrist University Hospital; University of Zurich
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-spinal-cord-motion-myelopathy-severity.html
Source: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00586-026-10522-1

A November 23, 2026 study analyzed MRI measurements from 112 patients with degenerative cervical myelopathy. Learned hierarchical classifiers identified compression at C3/4 as a severity-associated feature. Internal testing on 22 patients produced one additional correct classification. This single-center result supports a limited diagnostic association, without establishing causation, future disease progression or treatment benefit.

An exploratory preprint applied elastic-net logistic regression to existing genomic data from 47 Plasmodium vivax infections detected in two neighboring Peruvian Amazon communities, including 12 people reporting recent local travel. Repeated nested cross-validation yielded an AUC of 0.625 (95% bootstrap interval 0.522–0.724), versus 0.529 (0.402–0.657) after restricting the sample to non-travelers. This supports a bounded finding that fine-scale assignment was weak and sensitive to sample composition in this dataset. The analyses used different, overlapping infection sets, so their comparison does not isolate a causal effect of travel. Self-reported travel did not establish infection origin; intervals were conditional on saved predictions, and no independent cohort or operational surveillance benefit was tested.

## Cohort audit finds unstable performance in efferocytosis-related prognostic scores

A retrospective audit rebuilt an efferocytosis-related head-and-neck-cancer prognostic analysis in 519 primary tumors after detecting non-primary rows in the original cohort. ## Mathematician and Claude release a Lean proof of the Riemann hypothesis
2026-11-20 · mathematics · Anthropic
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-claude-riemann-hypothesis.html
Source: https://alpo.ge/remark.pdf

Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, released a Lean library of about 17 million lines that he states proves the Riemann hypothesis and the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, developed with Claude. His accompanying note says he guided the argument from a toy setting while Claude supplied much of the technical work, including the √X length of a chain of theta lifts; the note's timeline runs from 6 October to 16 November 2026. A day after release, the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative certified that the library proves Mathlib's statement of the Riemann hypothesis and passes several independent proof checkers. No human-readable proof has been published, and Alpöge writes that he has not yet mastered parts of the argument.

## Predicted enzyme structures support shared substrate gates in C-glycosylation

Analysis of structural models for 56 C-active UGT enzymes found acceptor gates throughout the set and two enzymes lacking a discernible donor gate; AlphaFold3 and source-labeled RobettaFold models supported variable open/closed gate conformations. ## Bayesian modeling estimates configuration-dependent uncertainty in printed PLA bending

A Research Square preprint trained a Bayesian physics-informed neural network on bending data from 60 groups of printed PLA specimens and combined it with finite-element simulation. A twelve-week teaching study randomized four matched pairs of university tutorial classes to a vocabulary application or non-adaptive word lists. A PointNet++ model learned to reconstruct maxillary denture-base geometry from paired scans of 79 patients’ edentulous maxillae and existing dentures, using 57 training, seven validation and 15 test cases. Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-study-do-student-perceptions-mirror-reality-a-mixed-methods-study-to-evaluate-the-accuracy-utility-an.html
Source: https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11455953/v1

Two introductory mathematics courses were studied using Gemini 2.5 Pro to draft scores/feedback from submissions and course references. Study One compared human-only (159 students) with human-curated AI (89); Study Two compared AI, peer and professor feedback. Grades were broadly similar, but students rated professor feedback most useful and read AI feedback less often (57% vs 89%/94%). This is a specific educational study, bounded to two courses and short-term feedback rather than learning outcomes.

## SPARC adaptive model composition guides an oxygen-evolution catalyst campaign

SPARC combines competing regression model families through out-of-fold predictions and sparse posterior composition, using predictive dispersion to set trust for exploration. Four clusters were identified. ## GPT-6 Astra constructs mutually orthogonal Latin squares that improve lower bounds at 33 orders
2026-11-12 · mathematics · Christopher D. Rosin (Constructive Codes; independent research project)
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-gpt-6-astra-constructs-mutually-orthogonal-latin-squares-that-improve-lower-bounds-at-33-orders.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2611.16299

GPT-6 Astra produced explicit mutually orthogonal Latin-square constructions that improve known lower bounds for N(n) at 33 values of n from 22 through 494. The standout construction gives four MOLS of order 22, completing the last open case needed to show N(n)≥4 for every n>10. Neural variational Monte Carlo wave functions, benchmarked against multiband exact diagonalization on small systems, were used to map phases in the Aharonov–Casher continuum model up to 36 electrons. At filling 2/3 the calculations identified an incommensurate electron Wigner crystal and a triangular hole-crystal phase; the study also estimated a uniform-field Jain-state freezing threshold. This is theoretical and model-specific, with no direct experimental confirmation. This concerns the Aharonov–Casher model and is distinct from the active artificial-graphene paired-Wigner-crystal result.

## Sparse constrained model discovery identifies isotropic material limit surfaces
2026-11-11 · materials · Technical University of Darmstadt
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-sparse-isotropic-material-limit-surfaces.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15476v1

The study compares sparse invariant libraries and physically gated mixtures of experts for fitting physically admissible yield and failure surfaces. Across five experimental datasets, richer invariant terms substantially improved the concrete fit (fourfold lower cross-validated error) and a selected TSSA surface combined a maximum-principal-stretch criterion with a cavitation term. The work also identifies substantial model-form uncertainty: hydrostatic tensile strength is weakly constrained, and the proposed quantitative Weibull interpretation is not supported by replicate data.

## Neural-potential simulations clarify a phosphonium/HFIP catalyst for CO2 conversion
2026-11-05 · chemistry · University of Alicante; University of Almería; University of Salerno; University of Camerino
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-neural-potential-phosphonium-hfip-catalyst.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1021/acsomega.6c07310

Researchers synthesized phosphonium-salt/HFIP catalysts for converting CO2 and epoxides into cyclic carbonates, reporting yields of 86–96% for monosubstituted and 66–88% for disubstituted epoxides at 25 °C and 1 atm CO2. Matlantis PFP v5.0.0, a trained neural interatomic potential, sampled the liquid-mixture structure; radial-distribution analysis supported strong association between HFIP and bromide. AI supported characterization of the new catalytic system; catalyst preparation and performance were experimentally established.

## Closed-loop machine learning maps multimetallic glucose-oxidation catalysts
2026-11-05 · chemistry · University of Bern
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-multimetallic-glucose-oxidation-electrocatalysts.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1039/d6ey00174b

Gaussian process regression surrogates trained on measured data guided which Au-Ir-Pt-Pd-Rh-Ru nanoparticle compositions to electrodeposit and test next. Highly active compositions lay near the Au-Pt edge, while the most poisoning-resistant were central with Rh and Pd up to 20 at%, revealing an activity versus poisoning-resistance trade-off. The loop's own experiments are the validation, without separate holdout, and only alkaline glucose oxidation was studied.

The study combines machine learning, metabolic networks and phylogenomics to date 14 forms of metabolism and six other traits. ## AlphaFold-Multimer predicts 2,895 interactions among human mitochondrial proteins

Texas A&M AgriLife Research screened 630,003 protein pairs from about 1,100 human mitochondrial proteins with AlphaFold-Multimer and identified 2,895 likely interactions, more than half not previously reported, giving 85 uncharacterized proteins their first probable partners. Random train/test splitting ignored spatial and temporal dependence, reporting may be incomplete, and hypothetical warming outputs are unmeasured sensitivity scenarios.

## AI-guided focused ultrasound and deep learning detect aortic stenosis in novices
2026-11-01 · medicine · Mayo Clinic
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-ai-guided-focus-ultrasound-aortic-stenosis.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1001/jamacardio.2026.3829

A deep learning algorithm was developed on 6753 Mayo Clinic patients to detect moderate or greater aortic stenosis and reached AUROC 0.99 in the internal test cohort and in Arizona and Florida validation cohorts. In a prospective cohort of 1302 examinations by novice operators using AI-guided focused cardiac ultrasound, 96.6% were suitable for automated analysis, with sensitivity 93% and specificity 96%. Positive predictive value was 49.4% before expert review of AI-positive and uninterpretable examinations and 91.1% after. All sites belong to one health system.

## Active learning finds an opposing-cosolvent electrolyte for aqueous zinc-ion batteries
2026-11-01 · materials · Seoul National University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-active-learning-zinc-ion-tri-solvent-electrolyte.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.6c20703

An extended active-learning framework clustered co-solvent candidates by molecular properties, selected co-solvents and optimized pairwise formulations for tri-solvent aqueous zinc-ion electrolytes with minimal experiments. It found a nonintuitive composition combining co-solvents with opposing properties, which disrupts the hydrogen-bonded network and reconstructs the solvation structure. Zn||NH4V4O10 full cells retained 90.2% capacity after 1,000 cycles. The abstract reports one formulation.

## OpenULF: A Modular Toolkit Enables Data-Driven Ultra-Low-Field MRI with both Classical and Quantum Sensors
2026-11-01 · multidisciplinary · Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of Minnesota, Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-11-2611-01511.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2611.01511v1

In one SQUID simulation at 50 µT, a UNet using four averages reached approximately the same PSNR as SimpleCNN using twenty. The separate modeled SQUID–coil crossover was mainly a sensor-physics effect. ## SMFNet diffusion model links single-molecule chromatin states to TF assemblies
2026-10-31 · biology · European Molecular Biology Laboratory
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-smfnet-combinatorial-tf-assembly.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.30.762954

SMFNet, a generative diffusion model, predicts distributions of single-molecule chromatin accessibility profiles from DNA sequence, and PRISM identifies sequence features tied to individual states. Experimental perturbation of the associated motifs redistributed states as SMFNet predicted. In silico motif screens showed that transcription factors differ in accessible-region width and nucleosome-positioning precision, and that motif combinations have partner- and spacing-dependent effects; natural variation at an endogenous element supported this in vivo. Only the abstract was reviewed.

PRISM-MPF used satellite microwave data to estimate pan-Arctic melt-pond fractions across eight melt seasons. Against an optical reference product, the model achieved a pooled R² of 0.532 and RMSE of 0.077, with weaker performance at high pond fractions.

## LHCb reports first single-experiment evidence for B⁰ → μ⁺μ⁻ decay
2026-10-30 · physics · LHCb Collaboration; CERN
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-lhcb-reports-first-single-experiment-evidence-for-b0-decay.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00230

Using 18 fb⁻¹ of Run 3 data and earlier LHCb data, the collaboration reports first single-experiment evidence for the rare B⁰→μ⁺μ⁻ decay, with a combined significance of 3.2σ and measured branching fraction (1.14 +0.42/−0.39 stat. +0.06/−0.05 syst.)×10⁻¹⁰. A boosted decision tree classified candidates and suppressed combinatorial background in the fit. This is evidence below the 5σ discovery threshold; results agree with Standard Model expectations. The date is the original preprint submission; CERN announced the result on 3 November 2026.

## GPT-6 Astra resolves the spectral isometry conjecture for arbitrary unital C*-algebras
2026-10-29 · mathematics · University of Cambridge; California Institute of Technology
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-gpt-6-astra-resolves-the-spectral-isometry-conjecture-for-arbitrary-unital-c-algebras.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40470

The paper proves that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between unital C*-algebras is a Jordan isomorphism; without unitality, such a map is a central-unitary multiple of a Jordan isomorphism. The proof establishes that entire one-parameter groups of unital spectral isometries are algebra automorphisms, then reduces the general case to the commutative case. The authors report that the result was formally verified in Lean.

## Symbolic regression and ML potentials guide a ferroelectric Dion-Jacobson perovskite
2026-10-27 · materials · National University of Singapore
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-ferroelectric-dion-jacobson-perovskite-design.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-78928-5

Starting from 11 known ferroelectric Dion-Jacobson 2D hybrid perovskites, symbolic regression defined a descriptor-bounded region, and similarity-guided expansion with chemical filtering reduced 83,924 molecules to 1012 candidate spacers. Machine-learned interatomic-potential relaxation found 338 candidates retaining Dion-Jacobson connectivity, and sequential prioritization selected s-2-fluorobutane-1,4-diamine. ## Planar energetics do not determine twin persistence in nanocrystalline aluminium
2026-10-27 · physics · Not stated in the reviewed material
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-2610-37925.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37925

Two learned potentials that reproduce similar planar slip energetics predicted markedly different retained twin coverage (64% versus 14%) from the same precursor under identical loading. The analysis identifies moving-core forces, local traction orientation, and asynchronous partial-slip fronts as determinants that planar energetic descriptors miss. The paper benchmarks Al-QP against five existing models on published DFT data and uses paired first-principles defect calculations to check local forces and energy margins. The result is computational; no experimental confirmation is claimed.

## Cracking into RACS - I. Measuring the cosmic dipole in the RACS-low3 and RACS-mid1 radio surveys with simulation-based inference
2026-10-26 · astronomy · Australian National University; University of Western Australia

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35207v1

Simulation-based inference applied to two Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey bands found radio-galaxy count dipoles inconsistent with the cosmic microwave background kinematic dipole. ## ESM-2-based screening finds yak collagen peptides that inhibit MMP-1
2026-10-22 · biology · Jilin University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-yak-collagen-anti-aging-peptides-mmp1.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41538-026-01223-6

AgeAttnMLP, an ESM-2-based screening model, reached AUC 0.891 under five-fold cross-validation and 0.879 under a cluster-aware grouped evaluation. Screening yak collagen sequences with in silico Alcalase hydrolysis identified TGPPGPSGI, GEPGAPGE and GPSGEPGTA as lead peptides. GEPGAPGE showed the strongest MMP-1 inhibition (IC50 126 ug/mL), and all three peptides extended Caenorhabditis elegans lifespan, most for GPSGEPGTA at 7.5 mg/mL. Potency is modest and in vivo evidence is limited to worms.

## The Virtual Biotech: a multi-agent AI framework for drug development decisions
2026-10-22 · medicine · Stanford University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-virtual-biotech-agents.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aeg6779

The Virtual Biotech journal abstract reports a human-guided multi-agent analysis of 55,984 trials. Drugs targeting cell-type-specific genes were associated with a 48% greater likelihood of reaching market and 32% fewer adverse events. The system also proposed a lung-cancer strategy and inferred possible reasons for a terminated ulcerative-colitis trial. These are retrospective associations and hypotheses, not demonstrated treatment benefits. The date represents the 2026-10-22 journal version; the linked preprint, including the same reported association, first appeared on 2026-02-23.

## A trained transformer approximated Heavy-Ball updates without examples of them
2026-10-22 · computer science · The University of Hong Kong
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-transformer-learns-heavy-ball-without-heavy-ball-examples.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31089

A theoretical and numerical study found that a simplified transformer for linear regression can shift from imitating gradient descent to approximating the known Heavy-Ball method. It first learned gradient-descent trajectories and was then trained against the true regression weights, without Heavy-Ball trajectories as supervision. The proof concerns later steps under specific initialization, parameter and high-dimensional data assumptions. The result appeared in arXiv v1 on October 22.

## Surface-informed active learning selects a tested Ni55Co10Fe35 oxygen-evolution catalyst
2026-10-22 · materials · Kyonggi University; Seoul National University; Dongguk University; Korea University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-surface-active-learning-nicofe-oxygen-evolution.html
Source: https://advanced.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/advs.78281

Researchers used Gaussian-process active learning with DFT adsorption energies to select a nickel–cobalt–iron alloy precursor. Synthesized Ni55Co10Fe35 required 327 mV overpotential at 10 mA/cm² in alkaline laboratory tests, versus 380 mV for NiFe and 404 mV for CoFe controls. Its Tafel slope was 43.07 mV/decade. Prediction and experimental activity maps did not fully agree; this supports compositional narrowing, not quantitative performance prediction. The working surface reconstructs into oxyhydroxides, which the alloy-surface model does not represent.

## Learned image analysis identifies interstitial zirconium in alloyed ceria films

A random-forest classifier trained on simulated electron-microscopy reconstructions helped distinguish isolated from overlapping zirconium interstitials in measured alloyed-ceria films. Author-deposited primary data describe octahedral interstitial zirconium at roughly 10²⁰ cm⁻³ and associated local disorder. ## CNN detects small Strombolian eruptions in infrared images of Erebus lava lake

A CNN trained on more than 54,000 denoised multitemporal infrared images of the Erebus lava lake classified images as no, small or large eruption. ## Machine learning identifies SIK1 as an epilepsy driver validated in rat models
2026-10-22 · medicine · The First People's Hospital of Qinzhou; The First Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi Medical University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-sik1-epilepsy-machine-learning.html
Source: https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42991733

Machine-learning screening of LKB1-pathway genes in GEO data prioritized SIK1. In a PTZ-induced rat epilepsy model, SIK1 knockdown delayed seizures and shortened their duration, whereas overexpression worsened severity. The paper abstract also reports that restoring downstream NR4A2 counteracted SIK1-related effects in rescue and neuronal experiments. ## GWAS and random forest give a 5-SNP sex identification panel for Pacific white shrimp
2026-10-22 · biology · Yellow Sea Fisheries Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Fishery Sciences
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-shrimp-sex-identification-5-snp-random-forest.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms27219409

In 1,244 Penaeus vannamei with a 55K SNP array, GWAS found 18 genome-wide significant SNPs and 10 candidate genes. A random forest 5-SNP panel was robust to simulated genotyping errors and missing data and gave 100% accuracy in two independent mixed-sex populations (ZJ, HN) and identified all females in an all-female cohort (MK). It is a marker panel, not a mechanism of sex determination.

## More specific wording narrowed semantic representations in four language models
2026-10-22 · computer science · Imperial College London

Researchers compared sentences that made a meaning more specific with sentences that merely added detail. Across four language models, the more specific versions formed tighter neighborhoods in model activation space. The pattern persisted after removing five dominant directions of variation.

## Deep learning model REED links DNA sequence to the destination of plant epimutations
2026-10-22 · biology · Chinese Academy of Sciences; Institute of Automation; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-reed-deep-learning-plant-methylation-set-point.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.21.760629

REED, a deep-learning model trained on one methylome, reads a per-CG-site methylation set point from DNA sequence. In pedigrees of seven Arabidopsis thaliana accessions, methylation gains concentrated at high set points and losses at low ones, and the equilibrium implied by their rates matched the set point. The set point also predicted germline epimutations in rice and changes in wild plants and a 330-year-old tree. The inferred rules (cooperation among nearby CG sites and transcription-factor motifs) are shared across flowering plants. Preprint; analysis of existing methylome data.

This retrospective proof of concept does not establish ship-compartment transfer, operational safety benefit or prospective performance.

## GPT-6 Pro proves a quadratic-size threshold suffices for random permutations to contain every length-n pattern
2026-10-09 · mathematics · Yu Chen; and Yiting Wang (affiliations not specified in arXiv record)
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-gpt-6-pro-proves-a-quadratic-size-threshold-suffices-for-random-permutations-to-contain-every-length-n-pattern.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13530

The paper proves that a uniformly random permutation of length 32n² contains every permutation of length n as a pattern with probability at least 1−exp(−c n/log n), for an absolute c>0 and sufficiently large n. This removes the prior log-log factor from the sufficient-length bound, resolves Alon’s open 1000n² problem, and establishes the correct Θ(n²) order.

## ATLAS graph neural network enables first LHC observation of single-top s-channel production
2026-10-08 · physics · ATLAS Collaboration; CERN

Source: https://atlas.cern/Updates/Briefing/Run2-Top-s-Channel

Using 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton collisions, ATLAS reports the first observation of single-top-quark s-channel production at the LHC, with 5.1σ observed (5.2σ expected) significance. ## GPT-6 Pro proves an optimal anticoncentration bound for polynomial Littlewood–Offord inequalities
2026-10-06 · mathematics · Alexandr Grebennikov (affiliation not stated in arXiv record)

The source presents a proof discovered autonomously by GPT-6 Pro establishing an O_d(r^{-1/2}) zero-probability bound for degree-d multilinear polynomials with r disjoint degree-d monomials, improving the prior bound by removing a polylogarithmic factor and resolving the Nguyen–Vu conjecture. ## Claude discovers algorithms that refute the 3SUM and APSP time-complexity hypotheses
2026-10-05 · computer science · Anthropic; Columbia University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-claude-discovers-algorithms-that-refute-the-3sum-and-apsp-time-complexity-hypotheses.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06783

Alman and Vassilevska Williams present deterministic algorithms for 3SUM on polynomial-size integers in O(n^1.9992) time and all-pairs shortest paths on directed graphs with polynomially bounded integer weights in O(n^2.9995) time, the first polynomial improvements over the textbook exponents. The paper says an internal Anthropic Claude research model discovered the algorithm autonomously; the human authors then understood, simplified, strengthened and extended it. ## GPT-6 Astra proves a linear coloring bound for graphs excluding clique minors
2026-10-04 · mathematics · University of British Columbia; University of Graz
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-10-gpt-6-astra-proves-a-linear-coloring-bound-for-graphs-excluding-clique-minors.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05291

The authors present a proof of the Linear Hadwiger conjecture: there is a constant C such that every graph with no K_t minor is colorable with at most Ct colors. GPT-6 Astra developed the proof after the authors directed it to the dense case and then asked it to bridge existing bounds; the resulting proof combines several known frameworks with a new bootstrap argument. The result is an asymptotic linear bound, not the stronger Hadwiger conjecture χ(G)≤h(G).

## AI-assisted proof establishes a dimension-independent KLS isoperimetric bound

Zhao Song and Xinzhi Zhang prove a universal, dimension-independent bound for the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits constant of isotropic log-concave probability measures, resolving the KLS conjecture. ## ML on partial-charge dynamics identifies residues driving mimochrome reactivity
2026-09-29 · chemistry · Massachusetts Institute of Technology
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-09-mimochrome-charge-dynamics-ml.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1039/d6sc05720a

Classical and ab initio molecular dynamics of three mimochrome artificial metalloenzymes were analysed with supervised machine-learning classifiers trained on partial-charge dynamics alone to tell the analogues apart. The classifiers flagged residues including Arg10', Lys11, Glu2' and Ser6', and a predicted Glu2'-Lys11 salt bridge was disrupted in a newly synthesised analogue, MC6*a-LysBoc, giving a seven-fold decrease in total turnover number. Quantum mechanical calculations indicate Arg10' stabilises the transition state for forming the reactive oxo. Machine learning is one step alongside molecular dynamics and quantum calculations, and only one analogue was tested.

Source: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/improving-synthesis-prediction-of-small-molecules-at-scale-with-retrochimera/

Published in Nature, the method combines a Transformer model (R-SMILES 2) and a template-based graph model (NeuralLoc) through a learned vote. In blind tests with expert chemists, 90% of complete routes were accepted, compared with 20–50% for the component models or a baseline, and nine of ten difficult targets were solved. ## GPT-assisted proof reduces Zieve’s Hurwitz realizability conjecture to the three-branch-point case
2026-09-20 · mathematics · School of Mathematical Sciences, University of Science and Technology of China; National Engineering Laboratory for Brain-inspired Intelligence Technology and Applications, University of Science and Technology of China
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-09-gpt-assisted-proof-reduces-zieves-hurwitz-realizability-conjecture-to-the-three-branch-point-case.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23663

The authors prove that, assuming Zieve-admissible branch data are realizable for three branch points, all such data with four or more branch points are realizable. This establishes that no additional obstruction arises solely from adding branch points; the underlying three-branch-point conjecture remains open. The paper discloses GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra assistance in exploring reduction strategies and in proof development and checking.

## LHCb observes the doubly charmed Ωcc⁺ baryon with an 8.7σ global significance
2026-09-18 · physics · LHCb Collaboration; CERN
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-09-lhcb-observes-the-doubly-charmed-cc-baryon-with-an-8-7-global-significance.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21921

Using 6.3 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV proton-proton collisions recorded in 2024, LHCb observed an Ωc⁰π⁺ mass peak with 8.7σ global significance and identified it as the weakly decaying doubly charmed Ωcc⁺ baryon. The reported mass is 3725.9 ± 1.0 (stat) ± 0.2 (syst) ± 0.4 (lifetime) ± 0.6 (external) MeV/c². A boosted decision tree suppressed random-track combinatorial background; the result is a preprint submitted to Physical Review Letters.

## GPT-5.6 constructs a counterexample to Talagrand’s operator cotype problem
2026-09-17 · mathematics · Xinglong Wu (author affiliation not stated in the arXiv record)
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-09-gpt-5-6-constructs-a-counterexample-to-talagrands-operator-cotype-problem.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19731

The paper gives a negative answer, already for q=2, to Talagrand’s question whether an operator’s Rademacher cotype is universally bounded by its Gaussian cotype and its (q,1)-summing norm. For every sufficiently large power-of-two dimension it constructs a Banach space and operator violating such a universal bound. The same construction also yields a negative answer to Kwapień’s decomposition problem.

## Paper2Agent integrates perturbation datasets to prioritize GPR137 at a psoriasis risk locus

Paper2Agent-generated agents used AlphaGenome to prioritize GPR137 as the top predicted gene affected by psoriasis-associated variant rs887314 in CD4+ T cells, then integrated that prediction with existing MPRA-coupled scCRISPRi and CD4+ T-cell Perturb-seq data. ## GPT-6 Astra finds a counting proof of the Erdős–Sós tree-embedding conjecture
2026-09-15 · mathematics · OpenAI FrontierMath Erdős project; exposition by David R. Wood (affiliation not stated in arXiv record)
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-09-gpt-6-astra-finds-a-counting-proof-of-the-erdossos-tree-embedding-conjecture.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17877

A counting argument proves that every finite graph with average degree greater than t−2 contains every tree on t vertices, resolving the Erdős–Sós conjecture. The proof counts adjacency-marked vertex orderings and uses an induction on the tree to bound those not supporting a rooted copy. The exposition states the sharp classical theorem and records its proof was discovered by GPT-6 Astra; a Lean repository checks the benchmark formalization of the result. Related expository papers of the same proof are aliases, not separate discoveries.

## AI-discovered proof resolves the Komlós vector-balancing conjecture
2026-09-10 · mathematics · Duke University; University of California, Irvine; independent research collaboration
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-09-ai-discovered-proof-resolves-the-komlos-vector-balancing-conjecture.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11189

The paper proves that for every finite family of Euclidean-norm-at-most-one vectors, signs can be chosen so the signed sum has infinity norm below 3√(2π), independent of vector count and dimension. It derives a corresponding square-root-in-sets bound for Beck–Fiala discrepancy. The authors explicitly credit the Odin Automatic AI Research Agent with discovering the proof; a separate elementary proof was posted independently. The algorithmic construction of such signings is a separate follow-up result and is not claimed here.

## AI-discovered construction improves the lower bound for the complex Grothendieck constant

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07000

The authors prove the classical complex Grothendieck constant exceeds 1.35584631827168, closing more than one quarter of the gap between Davie’s lower bound and Haagerup’s upper bound reported in the paper. ## GPT-5.6 helps prove an exact mapping between frustrated and field-driven spin chains
2026-08-31 · physics · Brookhaven National Laboratory
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-08-gpt-5-6-helps-prove-an-exact-mapping-between-frustrated-and-field-driven-spin-chains.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00322

A single-author preprint proves that every finite one-dimensional open O(n) spin chain with arbitrary inhomogeneous nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions has an exact, temperature-independent Hamiltonian mapping to a simpler nearest-neighbor chain with axial single-spin potentials. A parallel result for q-state Potts chains yields a closed-form solution for every q ≥ 2 and finite chain length. The theorem generalizes a 1990 Heisenberg-chain challenge and connects spontaneous collective behavior from competing interactions to field-induced behavior.

## A Lean proof establishes the two-sum Ruzsa–Turjányi limit
2026-08-28 · mathematics · Meta FAIR
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-08-ruzsa-turjanyi-two-fold-sumset-divergence.html

GPT-5.6 Sol proved that for a zero-density asymptotic additive basis, the ratio of the number of two-term sums up to 2N to the number of basis elements up to N tends to infinity. The statement is the two-sum variant of the older Ruzsa–Turjányi result for three-term sums.

A weakly supervised framework predicted PCR-confirmed Helicobacter pylori resistance from gastric biopsy whole-slide images in a multicenter cohort of 755 patients. ## Machine-learning triage identifies a dormant wandering black hole in a galaxy’s outskirts
2026-07-27 · astronomy · University of Maryland; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; University of California Observatories and collaborators

Source: https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/ae77f3

The off-nuclear transient TDE 2025abcr revealed a dormant supermassive black hole about 9.3 kiloparsecs from its host galaxy’s center, with a mass described as similar to the Milky Way’s central black hole. A machine-learning program searching for tidal-disruption flares anywhere in the sky selected the event for follow-up three months after deployment; astronomers then collected multi-instrument evidence and interpreted it as the strongest known wandering-black-hole case. ## AI-guided proof search solves five open problems in Banach space theory
2026-07-19 · mathematics · Lancaster University; University of Bern
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-07-ai-guided-proof-search-solves-five-open-problems-in-banach-space-theory.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17388

A research project used ChatGPT 5.5 Pro and Codex agents to develop proof ideas and proofs for five Banach-space problems. The resulting paper gives affirmative solutions to questions on toroidal Elton–Odell separation, non-Calkin unital Banach algebras, strict cosingularity and adjoints, weakly compact basis factorization, and primariness of Lp(L1). The authors report that models generated the core mathematics; human mathematicians checked and refined the proofs. The results are presented in an unrefereed preprint, and the authors take responsibility for correctness.

## Deep-learning splice prediction links a PARP2 variant to altered protein isoforms and influenza susceptibility
2026-07-18 · biology · Duke University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-07-deep-learning-splice-prediction-links-a-parp2-variant-to-altered-protein-isoforms-and-influenza-susceptibility.html
Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13663244/

By combining single-cell splicing-QTL analysis during influenza A infection with SpliceAI/Pangolin annotation and statistical fine-mapping, researchers prioritized causal splice variants. They experimentally characterized rs2297616 in PARP2: its A allele creates an alternative 5′ splice donor, adding 39 nucleotides and producing a protein isoform 13 amino acids longer. CRISPR-edited A549 cells showed the predicted splice and protein changes; the A-allele edited cells also had higher influenza A infection than G-allele cells. ## Claude-assisted analytic proof establishes a+b=1 for mean-field jamming exponents
2026-07-01 · mathematics · Sapienza University of Rome; CNR-Nanotec Rome; INFN Sezione di Roma 1; Beihang University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-07-claude-assisted-analytic-proof-establishes-a-b-1-for-mean-field-jamming-exponents.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1088/1742-5468/ae7bd7

Giorgio Parisi and Francesco Zamponi provide an analytic proof that the critical exponents a and b in the full replica-symmetry-breaking scaling solution for infinite-dimensional dense hard spheres obey a+b=1. The identity links gap, contact-force and overlap scaling relations and had previously been known numerically but not analytically. The authors report that Claude Opus 4.7 derived the core proof idea with minimal supervision, with Sonnet 4.6 helping refine it; the authors found and corrected errors in an early draft, then verified and edited the final proof.

The HOLISMOKES search identified the ZTF transient SN 2025wny at the position of the previously selected lens candidate PS1 J0716+3821. Follow-up imaging resolved multiple supernova images and spectroscopy classified it as a Type I superluminous supernova at z=2.008 ± 0.001; the second deflector galaxy was measured spectroscopically at z=0.375 ± 0.001. This is the first confirmed galaxy-scale strongly lensed supernova with expected time delays of days to weeks, offering a new system for time-delay cosmography.

## Inverse optimal control infers shared and patient-specific squat objectives after knee replacement

Bi-level inverse optimal control inferred individual and shared movement-objective weights from recorded squats in six people after total knee replacement. 2026-06-15 · biology · Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory; Johns Hopkins University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-06-fungai-antifungal-peptides.html
Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13289945/

Fung-AI combines a generative adversarial network with learned antifungal and hemolysis classifiers to select peptides for testing. The study first tested five peptides from separate clusters; activity of peptide 40 prompted testing of eight more members from cluster 17. Five of the nine tested cluster-17 peptides inhibited Fusarium graminearum, a post-selection cluster-specific outcome—not a general 5/13 model hit rate. Four peptides showed activity against Candida albicans, while none inhibited C. auris up to 500 μg/mL. The paper’s HepG2 cytotoxicity statements are internally inconsistent for peptide 48 and peptide 65, and peptide 12 and 40 have reported cytotoxicity; these assays establish neither human safety nor clinical efficacy.

## Cross-linking mass spectrometry guided structure prediction of disordered Encephalitozoon hellem proteins
2026-06-12 · biology · Department of Pathology, Albert Einstein College of Medicine, New York, New York, USA; Department of Pathogenic Biology, School of Basic Medical Sciences, Cheeloo College of Medicine, Shandong University, Jinan, Shandong, China; Department of Biochemistry, Albert Einstein College of Medicine, New York, New York, USA; Department of Systems & Computational Biology, Albert Einstein College of Medicine, New York, New York, USA; Department of Genetics, Albert Einstein College of Medicine, New York, New York, USA; Department of Medicine, Albert Einstein College of Medicine, New York, New York, USA
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-06-1128-mbio-02261-26.html
Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13753748/

Predicted a previously unreported Swp1b–EnP1 interaction/interface in the E. hellem spore wall; the restraint-guided model differs from low-confidence AlphaFold3 predictions and gives structural hypotheses for their interface. Three XL-MS runs supplied restraints; a fourth independent DSSO XL-MS run showed 51/68 links within 26 Å and 57/68 within 30 Å of the model. Authors also report that heterologous yeast-two-hybrid/co-IP attempts did not detect the interaction, no genetic perturbation system exists, and stoichiometry is assumed rather than established. Preprint abstract (PubMed PMID 42327317) dated 2026-06-12 already contains the same result; peer-reviewed journal version 2026-10-20. A preprint posted 2026-06-12 contained the result before the October 2026 journal version; attempted yeast-two-hybrid/co-immunoprecipitation did not detect the interaction, so the interface remains a model-supported hypothesis.

The June 2026 bioRxiv version describes an initial machine-learning-guided screen of ZINC20 compounds balancing predicted antibacterial activity, mammalian-cell toxicity, and mechanism-of-action novelty. ## AI-designed bacterial anti-defense proteins enable phage infection and plasmid retention

RFdiffusion-based de novo binder design and experimental screening produced synthetic proteins that inhibited three bacterial defense systems: Thoeris and Avs1 in Bacillus subtilis assays, and DdmDE in Vibrio cholerae. ## Machine learning shows hepatocyte-like cell lines poorly reproduce primary liver enhancer activity
2026-06-09 · biology · Carnegie Mellon University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-06-hepatocyte-cell-line-regulatory-landscapes.html
Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.06.05.730479v1

The authors compared four immortalized hepatocyte-like cell lines with primary liver tissue using chromatin-accessibility assays, motif analysis and a previously trained multi-species liver-enhancer classifier. Classifier sensitivity was below 60% on the cell-line enhancers; only HepG2 exceeded 50%, supporting the bounded finding that these lines incompletely reproduce native liver regulatory landscapes. Modifying AML12 culture conditions did not substantially improve similarity. The first preprint version already reports this result on 9 June 2026; a later version was posted 22 November. The result concerns selected cell lines and enhancer datasets, not every liver experiment, and classifier output is an indirect readout of regulatory similarity rather than direct proof of enhancer function.

## Deep learning reveals 21 previously uncataloged slow-slip events at Parkfield
2026-06-09 · physics · GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences; RWTH Aachen University; EarthScope Consortium; Stanford University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-06-deep-learning-parkfield-slow-slip.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-74095-9

An unsupervised neural autoencoder and clustering helped identify 21 short slow-slip events absent from a manual catalog of historical borehole strain records on the San Andreas Fault near Parkfield. Nearby creepmeters recorded corresponding slip for 14 of the new events. In the retrospective study, nearby low-frequency earthquakes were more frequent around slow-slip events, with enhanced activity immediately following slow-slip onset. Composition-based machine-learning models screened salt-hydration reactions, after which researchers synthesized and measured selected candidates by differential scanning calorimetry. ## Machine-learning seismicity maps a 250-km eastern edge of the subducted Yakutat microplate

An expanded machine-learning earthquake catalog and complementary receiver-function and ambient-noise images reveal a previously unrecognized, roughly 250-km linear cluster of about 1,750 earthquakes that the authors interpret as tracing the northeastern/eastern edge of the subducted Yakutat microplate beneath south-central Alaska. Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-machine-learning-mapping-finds-broader-preservation-of-pre-glacial-landscapes-across-arctic-canada-and-greenland.html
Source: https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2025JF008661

A random-forest model using six terrain morphometrics from ArcticDEM classified glacial erosional styles across Arctic Canada and Greenland. The map indicates that regions with little or no glacial erosion, and thus potentially preserved pre-glacial landscape fragments, occur more widely than previous mapping recognized; it also finds distinct morphologies between Greenland and Canada. The authors infer that inherited topography, ice dynamics, latitude and geology help shape these patterns.

## Machine-learning-assisted design predicts Netsene, a 3D carbon nodal-surface semimetal
2026-05-21 · materials · Authors’ institutions include Nanjing University and associated materials-physics groups (see arXiv record)
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-machine-learning-assisted-design-predicts-netsene-a-3d-carbon-nodal-surface-semimetal.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22141

A theory-guided inverse-design study combined a crystal diffusion variational autoencoder with a Crystal Transformer to propose a body-centered tetragonal C24 allotrope, Netsene. First-principles calculations report dynamical and mechanical stability and a nested nodal-surface semimetal band structure with drumhead surface states. This is a computationally predicted allotrope and electronic phase, not an experimentally synthesized material.

## AI-driven formal proof search resolves Erdős problems and OEIS conjectures
2026-05-21 · mathematics · Google DeepMind
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-deepmind-erdos-oeis-formal-search.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763

An agent that alternates LLM proof generation with Lean verification autonomously resolved 9 of 353 open Erdős problems and proved 44 of 492 OEIS conjectures, at a cost of a few hundred dollars per problem according to the abstract. Proofs are Lean-verified, so the checking is mechanical; the abstract does not name the system and the results are limited to the problem sets tested.
