## AI generates compounds with experimentally validated pancreatic cancer cell selectivity
2026-05-20 · chemistry · Institute for Research in Biomedicine (IRB Barcelona), The Barcelona Institute of Science and Technology; ICREA
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-ai-generates-compounds-with-experimentally-validated-pancreatic-cancer-cell-selectivity.html
Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42162204/

The IRB Barcelona team trained cell-line cytotoxicity predictors on data from more than 11,000 compounds assayed across pancreatic-cancer and control cell lines, then integrated the models with a reinforcement-learning generative system to design molecules for cell-selective effects. In follow-up tests, 45 AI-designed molecules or close analogues were assayed; 20 showed the intended cell-specific cytotoxicity, and dose-response testing confirmed 18 of those 20. Across the seven selectivity exercises, at least one hit was found in five; measured IC50 values could be calculated for 12 confirmed hits and ranged from 0.97 to 16.6 μM in the targeted cell lines.

## WeatherNext and Hurricane Melissa: earlier warning in Jamaica
2026-05-19 · climate · Google DeepMind
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-weathernext-melissa.html
Source: https://deepmind.google/blog/how-weathernext-helped-the-national-hurricane-center-better-predict-hurricane-melissas-historic-landfall-in-jamaica/

WeatherNext forecast a Category 5 landfall in Jamaica five days ahead with 80% probability, rising to nearly 100% at three days. According to the post, it was the best single model for track and intensity in the National Hurricane Center's 2025 verification report, which used it alongside its HAFS model. The post gives no numerical comparisons; rapid intensification remains very hard to predict.

## Co-Scientist: repurposed drugs against liver fibrosis

In Gary Peltz's Stanford lab, two of the three existing drugs proposed by Co-Scientist blocked fibrosis and promoted regeneration in human liver cells, while Peltz's own two choices showed no benefit. ## Unsupervised learning separates rockfall and glacier-sliding precursors before the Blatten collapse
2026-05-15 · physics · Université Grenoble Alpes; Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris; University of Tokyo; Service des dangers naturels, Valais
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-unsupervised-learning-separates-rockfall-and-glacier-sliding-precursors-before-the-blatten-collapse.html
Source: https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2025GL121175

Unsupervised clustering of 20 days of seismic data before the 28 May 2025 Blatten glacier collapse separated rockfall signals from events associated with basal glacier sliding. Sliding-related event counts accelerated approximately exponentially beginning about five days before collapse, with further acceleration about 1.5 days beforehand; the authors interpret this pattern as consistent with nucleation-like slip weakening.

## Spectroscopic follow-up revises Gaia machine-learning white-dwarf classifications and reveals a large magnetic and carbon-rich population
2026-05-15 · astronomy · Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya; Universitat de Barcelona and collaborators
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-spectroscopic-follow-up-revises-gaia-machine-learning-white-dwarf-classifications-and-reveals-a-large-magnetic-and-carbon-rich-population.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16493

Follow-up spectra for 255 Gaia white dwarfs were compared with machine-learning classifications from low-resolution Gaia spectra. The study reports that only 5 of 112 objects classified as massive DBs were genuine DB white dwarfs; most were magnetic white dwarfs or warm DQ stars. Its spectroscopy also catalogued 63 magnetic white dwarfs and 29 warm DQs in the selected sample, while confirming high classification accuracy for major spectral types within the classifier’s training set.

## Machine learning guides a near-infrared Mo/Sb halide phosphor
2026-05-15 · materials · Guangxi University; South China University of Technology
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-ml-guided-mo-sb-nir-phosphor.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-73105-0

A regression model trained on experimental and theoretical data guided Mo/Sb/Br co-doping for a lead-free near-infrared phosphor. The authors report synthesizing Cs₂Zr(Cl₀.₄₆Br₀.₅₄)₆:12%Mo⁴⁺/3.6%Sb³⁺, with emission near 920 nm, internal quantum efficiency of 92.4%, and external quantum efficiency of 65.9% under the reported conditions. Its measured intensity was about 20% higher than the authors’ orthogonal-design comparator. A separate diffusion model was used for image reconstruction demonstrations; this does not establish clinical diagnostic performance. Earlier composition-level prior art and independent replication remain open.

## Machine learning prioritizes compounds active against heterogeneous glioblastoma stem-cell models
2026-05-13 · medicine · University of Edinburgh; and Cancer Research UK Scotland Centre
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-machine-learning-prioritizes-compounds-active-against-heterogeneous-glioblastoma-stem-cell-models.html

Researchers trained cell-survival predictors on image-based screening data from six patient-derived glioblastoma stem-cell lines and screened more than 12,000 compounds. Experimental follow-up identified three compounds with activity across the GBM phenotype; HSP90 inhibitor XL-888 eliminated all six tested lines at nanomolar IC50 values, with analyses consistent with HSP90 inhibition and downstream client-protein disruption.

The MISPOP ensemble screened a natural peptide library of 1,033 sequences, prioritized 16 oncolytic-peptide candidates and selected five for synthesis and testing. ## MatterSim and tantalum phosphide as a good heat conductor
2026-05-12 · materials · Microsoft Research
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-mattersim-tap.html
Source: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/advancing-ai-for-materials-with-mattersim-experimental-synthesis-faster-simulation-and-multi-task-models/

A candidate identified with MatterSim-v1, tetragonal tantalum phosphide, was synthesized and showed thermal conductivity of 152 W/m/K in the best samples, close to silicon. MatterSim-v1 inference is 3–5 times faster, and the new multi-task model MatterSim-MT predicts energies, forces, and properties. Battery and other property results are predictions, not experimental confirmations.

## Machine-learning metabolomics identifies widespread promiscuous activities in Escherichia coli enzymes
2026-05-12 · biology · ETH Zurich; Weizmann Institute of Science; University Children’s Hospital Zurich and University of Zurich
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-machine-learning-metabolomics-identifies-widespread-promiscuous-activities-in-escherichia-coli-enzymes.html
Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13389410/

In vitro metabolomics of 667 purified E. coli enzymes, analyzed with a machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, indicated previously unrecognized promiscuous activities in 11% of enzymes tested. Follow-up reconstruction assigned 22 reaction stoichiometries to 11 enzymes, with four reactions experimentally validated; examples include expanded nucleotide-substrate use by DeoA, cofactor and sugar promiscuity in NanK, and FMN dephosphorylation by CobC. Follow-up assays also found that pyrimidine-specific ribonucleoside hydrolase RihB acted on thymidine, guanosine and deoxyuridine, further extending its measured substrate range.

## Machine-learning earthquake catalog reveals scale-dependent fault controls at Gonghe geothermal site
2026-05-12 · physics · Southern University of Science and Technology; Institute of Geomechanics, Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences; ETH Zürich
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-machine-learning-earthquake-catalog-reveals-scale-dependent-fault-controls-at-gonghe-geothermal-site.html
Source: https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2025JB033158

A machine-learning workflow catalogued 7,346 microearthquakes (ML −2.0 to 2.18) recorded during 2021 stimulation and circulation tests at China’s Gonghe enhanced-geothermal-system site. The catalog resolves a ring-shaped distribution with four clusters and varying faulting styles. The authors infer that site-scale seismicity reactivated mapped, pre-existing natural faults; at borehole scale, the principal seismogenic zone coincides with strong SHmax rotation. Stress modeling estimates a low fault-friction coefficient near 0.23 (95% CI 0.19–0.48) and the low-to-moderate fluid overpressure needed for slip.

## Machine learning designs bulk metallic glasses with peak hardness near 2,450 HV
2026-05-12 · materials · Max Planck Institute for Sustainable Materials
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-hard-metallic-glasses-vibann.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-73008-0

VIBANN used a dataset of 673 bulk metallic-glass compositions to guide the design of five alloys, synthesized as amorphous 2 mm rods. The paper's experimental results identify alloy A1, B68Nb24Fe4W4, as the hardest: 2,447 +/- 44 HV at a 0.5 N indentation load, with six replicate indentations. Hardness decreases with increasing load; the peak is not a value for every alloy or test condition. X-ray scattering and molecular dynamics support a structural interpretation within the studied composition range. The date refers to the May 2026 paper, rather than the institute's later August announcement.

## AI-assisted analysis reveals retrospective seismicity before the Dingri earthquake
2026-05-11 · physics · Istituto Nazionale di Oceanografia e di Geofisica Sperimentale (OGS)
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-phase-net-reveals-retrospective-dingri-seismicity.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-49197-5

A PhaseNet-assisted workflow combined phase detection, polarisation analysis and template matching on records from one permanent station to reconstruct seismicity in the two years before the 2025 Mw 7.1 Dingri earthquake. The authors report increased event rate and clustering beginning about 45 days before the mainshock. This retrospective pattern is interpreted as compatible with late-stage nucleation; the study does not establish a prospective earthquake forecast.

## AlphaFold homodimer predictions link truncation to different interface outcomes
2026-05-09 · biology · Istanbul University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-alphafold-homodimer-truncation-structural-grammar.html
Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.05.06.723091v1.full.pdf

The May 9, 2026 preprint version compared 5,168 canonical/truncated human homodimer prediction pairs using AlphaFold-Multimer structures and interface-confidence scores. Among 234 pairs with high-confidence canonical homodimers, it classified 132 as conserved, 61 as interface-ablated and 41 as partially destabilized. These are computational classifications, without biochemical or cellular confirmation of the specific dimers. The later deposited abstract retains these headline proportions but revises interpretations of apparent interface emergence; those emergence and disorder claims are outside this entry.

## Unsupervised seismicity categories distinguish documented preparatory phases before three large earthquakes
2026-05-04 · physics · GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences; University of Potsdam; University of Naples Federico II; University of Genoa; Stanford University; international collaborators
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-05-unsupervised-seismicity-categories-distinguish-documented-preparatory-phases-before-three-large-earthquakes.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-72279-x

A K-means framework grouped earthquake families by catalog-derived spatial, temporal, magnitude and seismo-mechanical features. Retrospective analyses found highly localized families with higher interaction and strain release before the 2023 Kahramanmaraş, 2009 L’Aquila and 2014 Iquique earthquakes; similar critical categories were absent before the 2016 Amatrice and 2024 Noto events, where no catalog-visible preparatory phase was detected. The work describes a conditional diagnostic, not a general earthquake prediction system.

A closed-loop microfluidic platform ran 120 experiments in one 12-hour campaign on double perovskite nanoplatelets with up to six elements and identified the brightest lead-free composition found in that campaign. The press release gives no numerical photoluminescence gain, so the improvement is not quantified in the sources checked. Validation is the authors' own experimental measurements, and the paper should be checked for the brightness figures.

A random forest combined gait, postural, neurophysiological and MRI measures in 75 people with clinically diagnosed functional motor disorders and 75 healthy controls. A transformer-based Siamese multimodal model combined PyRadiomics features and Med3D-pretrained ResNet101 features from pre- and post-treatment MRI in 440 patients with locally advanced rectal cancer from three centers. In the independent validation cohort it reached an AUC of 0.789, above early-fusion machine learning (0.629) and single-timepoint transformers (0.739 and 0.728). ## Random forest predicts 6-month unplanned hospitalization in long-term care residents
2026-04-30 · medicine · Anhui Medical University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-04-ltcf-hospitalization-random-forest-anhui.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.archger.2026.106284

A random forest using 11 routine-assessment predictors was built for 768 residents of 15 long-term care facilities in Anhui, China, of whom 253 (32.9%) had an unplanned hospitalization within 6 months. AUCs were 0.934 in a held-out test set, 0.953 and 0.869 in two external cohorts. Calibration varied across settings, the study is retrospective and from one province, and prospective implementation is still needed.

## Stacked machine-learning ensemble predicts coronary heart disease risk from routine data
2026-04-30 · medicine · Affiliated Hospital of Nantong University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-04-chd-risk-stacked-ensemble-framingham.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.3389/fcvm.2026.1821221

A stacked ensemble of gradient boosting, random forest and XGBoost with a logistic-regression meta-learner, trained on the Framingham cohort (n = 4,240), reached internal AUC 0.977 and, on a retrospective hospital cohort (n = 200), external AUC 0.929 and accuracy 0.885. SHAP identified systolic blood pressure, age, total cholesterol and fasting glucose among top predictors. ## CellOracle-guided pancreatic islet differentiation experiments reveal STAT1 and ZEB1 lineage roles
2026-04-30 · biology · Washington University School of Medicine; University of Miami
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-04-celloracle-guided-pancreatic-islet-differentiation-experiments-reveal-stat1-and-zeb1-lineage-roles.html
Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.04.27.721124v2.full

A digital model built from 400,603 cells across 61 single-cell datasets used CellOracle gene-regulatory-network inference and in-silico transcription-factor perturbations to nominate regulators of stem-cell-derived human islet differentiation. CRISPRi experiments supported a previously unreported role for STAT1 in exocrine specification: transient STAT1 knockdown reduced exocrine markers, and JAK–STAT inhibition preserved beta-cell markers and improved glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. CRISPRi also supported a stage-dependent role for ZEB1, whose early knockdown impaired endocrine specification and later knockdown reduced off-target serotonergic cells while increasing beta-cell proportion. The date is the first preprint posting; this entry summarizes the later version reviewed in the research record, which reports the specific STAT1 and ZEB1 experiments.

## Wearable-data models evaluate near-term binge-eating risk

Source: https://doi.org/10.1002/eat.70107

In a four-week observational study of 30 adults with recurrent binge eating, random-forest models used smartwatch physiology or self-reported affect to evaluate episode risk. The first three weeks trained models and the final week tested them within the same participants. ## Neural segmentation reveals persistent postsynaptic-density enlargement after potentiation
2026-04-11 · biology · University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-04-stardist-synapse-structure-camkii.html
Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.04.09.717511v1.full

In hippocampal slice neurons, StarDist neural-network segmentation identified postsynaptic densities for tracking over 16 hours. After CaMKII photoactivation, postsynaptic densities and spine heads enlarged rapidly; density enlargement persisted at 14 hours while spine-head expansion lasted about 6 hours. The original result was publicly posted on April 11, 2026, followed by a peer-reviewed version on November 20. The journal analysis included 6 activated and 5 control slice cultures, with thousands of nested synaptic measurements. Models were trained on a small manually annotated tile set and visually checked; held-out segmentation accuracy and independent replication were not reported.

## Erdős Problem #650 solved with ChatGPT strategy and Aristotle Lean proof
2026-03-30 · mathematics · Southeast University; Xi'an Jiaotong University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-03-erdos-650-aristotle.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28636

The authors prove f(m) = min(m, ceil(2 sqrt(m))) for all m, resolving Erdős Problem #650 on Bloom's site, where f(m) counts disjoint divisibility pairs in an interval for an m-element set. The detailed argument was formally verified in Lean by Harmonic's Aristotle, following a strategy proposed by ChatGPT. Caveat: arXiv preprint; the AI contribution is the strategy and formalization, not an independently checked autonomous solution.

## AI-designed protein family binds and senses small molecules, including cortisol
2026-03-28 · biology · KAIST; University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-70953-8

The study combines trRosetta-based scaffold hallucination and Rosetta design with ProteinMPNN/LigandMPNN sequence design and AlphaFold structural filtering to create NTF2-like binders for six small-molecule targets. ## ParticleNet enables first hadron-collider W-boson mass measurement from hadronic decays

Using 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton data, CMS reports the first measurement of the W-boson mass in an all-jets final state at a hadron collider: 80.83 ± 0.55 GeV. ## AI-assisted work proves a Latin-square imbalance bound, with optimal examples through order 52
2026-03-09 · mathematics · Cornell University; TU Wien
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-03-ai-assisted-work-proves-a-latin-square-imbalance-bound-with-optimal-examples-through-order-52.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.08322v2

A collaborative LLM-plus-symbolic-computation study proved that every n×n Latin square with n ≡ 1 (mod 3) has imbalance at least 4n(n−1)/9. It introduced near-perfect permutations that attain the bound and computationally found independently verified matching examples for every such order from 4 through 52. The universal lower-bound theorem was formally checked in Lean 4.

## First observation of single-top-quark production with a W and Z boson at CMS
2026-02-25 · physics · CMS Collaboration; CERN Large Hadron Collider
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-02-first-observation-of-single-top-quark-production-with-a-w-and-z-boson-at-cms.html
Source: https://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/TOP-24-009/

CMS reports the first observation of single-top-quark production in association with a W and Z boson in proton-proton collisions. A Particle Transformer classifier and improved reconstruction separated the rare tWZ signal from major backgrounds in three- and four-lepton events. Combining 13 and 13.6 TeV data (200 fb⁻¹), the measured signal has 5.8σ observed significance (3.5σ expected) and cross sections of 248 ± 52 fb at 13 TeV and 242 ± 77 fb at 13.6 TeV. The result agrees with the Standard Model within 2.3σ.

## Machine-learning analysis separates genetic from environmental drivers of stimulated cytokine responses in healthy adults

In 406 healthy GEOCODE cohort participants, whole-blood cytokine responses to Toll-like-receptor (TLR) and T-cell-receptor (TCR) stimulation varied across people, including high- and low-IL-6-response profiles associated with monocyte counts, sex and sampling season. Feature-importance analysis of machine-learning models found TCR-induced cytokine predictions were mainly driven by genetic features, whereas TLR-induced predictions were driven more by environmental and biological features. ## Deep-learning tracking of mantle simulations finds continental-margin subduction zones persist longer

A fully convolutional network segmented subduction zones in two-dimensional mantle-convection simulations using temperature, vertical velocity and fineness fields. ## LFAST: an LLM agent drives robotic synthesis of the new COF-2000 framework

A GPT-4o-based agent (LFAST) screened reaction conditions over a 96-condition matrix and refined them after each round, raising the crystallinity index of a reference covalent organic framework by 350% and yielding COF-2000, a previously unreported material with higher structural order. Publication date is taken from secondary reports of the JACS paper and should be checked against the journal page.

## Interpreted neural networks flag candidate schizophrenia loci in the Estonian Biobank
2026-02-23 · biology · Estonian Genome Centre, Institute of Genomics, University of Tartu; CNRS, INRIA, LISN, Paris-Saclay University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2026-02-ann-interpretability-flags-candidate-schizophrenia-loci-estonian-biobank.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1093/nargab/lqag019

Feedforward neural networks trained on genome-wide genotypes of 1,814 schizophrenia cases and 7,325 matched controls from the Estonian Biobank were interpreted post hoc (integrated gradients, with permuted-label models to estimate P-values) to flag potentially associated loci. One locus passed the strict threshold and seven loci (14 SNPs) the relaxed threshold, in regions not identified by the authors' linear baseline; the strongest overlaps a known bipolar-disorder locus. Only 6, 3 or 1 of 1,370 previously established schizophrenia loci were recovered, depending on the overlap rule. The authors report concordance with schizophrenia and bipolar-disorder loci and brain-related enrichment, but P-values were not well calibrated in a small type 1 diabetes test, no uncertainty quantification or ground truth exists, and replication in other populations and biobanks is still needed. The flagged loci are statistical candidates, not validated associations or treatment targets. This is primarily a method paper; the earlier arXiv preprint (2024) did not contain the schizophrenia analysis, so the journal version is dated.

The neural network scanned about 100 million cutouts from the Hubble Legacy Archive in roughly two and a half days: nearly 1,400 anomalies were flagged and over 1,300 confirmed, including more than 800 not previously documented in the literature (mergers, lenses, and jellyfish galaxies). ## Machine-learning seismic catalogue reveals a long-period swarm before Sierra Negra eruption onset

A machine-learning phase-picking and template-matching workflow expanded the catalogue for the 2018 Sierra Negra eruption onset, identifying a northwestern-caldera swarm of long-period microearthquakes missing from earlier manually picked records. ## Co-FunSearch finds adversarial instances raising the Best-Fit bin packing bound
2026-01-23 · computer science · University of Bonn; Google DeepMind; University of Manitoba

A human-LLM pipeline (Co-FunSearch) finds adversarial instances for heuristics, raising the lower bound for Best-Fit bin packing in the random-order model from 1.3 to 1.5. Using a high-throughput qPCR assay, Arizona State University researchers measured microRNA 5p/3p strand use across six Caenorhabditis elegans developmental stages and selected tissues. A machine-learning pipeline selected a seven-gene lactylation-related transcriptomic score (LDS) from nine Alzheimer disease cohorts. A structure-conditioned workflow combining CycleRFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN and HighFold generated and screened 1,500 cyclic peptide–TREM2 complexes and prioritized four candidates. The lead TP4 showed weak but reproducible TREM2 binding in spectral-shift, microscale-thermophoresis and surface-plasmon-resonance assays. The authors report favorable plasma stability and moderate metabolic stability, presenting the work as an initial proof of concept for TREM2-targeted cyclic binders.

## Diffusion-guided design tests bimetallic ammonia-decomposition catalysts
2025-12-19 · chemistry · Worcester Polytechnic Institute; University of California, Riverside; University of Massachusetts Lowell

Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12814173/

A diffusion model guided by a learned nitrogen-adsorption predictor generated bimetallic candidates near the target adsorption energy. Co75Mo25 was among the generated candidates and maps exactly to the tested Co3Mo1 ratio; under the reported supported-catalyst assay it reached 18.6 μmol gmetal⁻¹ s⁻¹ at 520 °C, about twice the paper’s Ru reference under its stated test. Co–Mo catalysts are established prior art, so this entry does not claim the first Co–Mo ammonia-decomposition catalyst or global composition novelty. A CRISPRi and single-cell RNA-sequencing screen tested 979 candidate enhancers in cultured human primary astrocytes and identified 158 functional enhancer–gene pairs, including enhancers regulating genes implicated in Alzheimer disease. ## Model-designed mutation paths switched WW-domain binding specificity

The first public preprint appeared on bioRxiv on 2025-12-10. Its reviewed version reports that designed WW-domain mutational paths largely retained binding, while the same mutations introduced in scrambled order disrupted function. The eLife reviewed-preprint v1 (2026-04-09) later quantified binding for 54 of 58 tested designs and described cross-reactive intermediates on some specificity transitions. ## The levers of political persuasion with conversational AI
2025-12-04 · multidisciplinary · University of Oxford; UK AI Security Institute; London School of Economics; Stanford University; MIT
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-12-levers-political-persuasion-ai.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aea3884

In three large experiments with 76,977 participants, 19 LLMs argued 707 British political positions in dialogue. Persuasiveness was driven mainly by information density, while tailoring to user traits added little, and post-training for persuasion raised effectiveness by up to 50%. The most persuasive models also produced the most inaccurate claims. Caveat: the persuasion effects are measured in survey experiments, and accuracy was tested on a subset of claims.

## Heat-resistant crops: a hybrid photosynthesis enzyme

At Michigan State University, AlphaFold predicted the 3D structure of glycerate kinase in a crop and a heat-loving alga. Replacing three flexible loops with rigid loops from the alga produced a hybrid that remained stable up to 65 °C. The enzyme has not yet been tested in whole plants.

## AI-guided subtilisin variants improve aqueous amide formation

Source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894725106992

The study reports that wild-type subtilisin BPN′ directly catalyzed condensation of free carboxylic acids and amines in aqueous PBS (pH 8, 40 °C), forming a peptide-bond amide without stoichiometric coupling reagents. AIRES combined probabilistic machine-learning predictions with robotic synthesis, optical crystal screening and single-crystal X-ray diffraction to explore zinc zeolitic imidazolate frameworks. ## GPT-5 helps solve a 40-year-old problem about Nesterov's accelerated gradient
2025-11-24 · mathematics · OpenAI; and University of California, Los Angeles
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-11-gpt5-nesterov.html
Source: https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-mathematical-discovery/

Ernest Ryu (UCLA) proved why Nesterov's accelerated gradient method, introduced in 1983, remains stable despite the extra momentum that makes it faster. GPT-5's turning point was a rewrite of the equations: not correct as given, but with a structure Ryu then developed and proved himself, over about twelve hours across three days and after a dozen approaches. OpenAI's account says the model created no new mathematical tools and often produced plausible arguments that failed verification.

## Machine-learning metabolomics identifies DHEAS and citrate signatures in anti-MDA5 dermatomyositis

## SPEAR and microfluidics discover antimicrobial peptides from isolated-habitat metagenomes

Source: https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.11.13.688364

MicroSPEAR combines SPEAR, a sequence-structure-aware ensemble predictor, with a microfluidic susceptibility platform that cuts testing time from about 18 h to 4 h. Applied to a catalogue from 4,480 metagenomes across 15 isolated habitat types, SPEAR identified 383,027 non-redundant candidate peptides, 63.1% without detectable homologues. ## Mind captioning: text descriptions of viewed videos decoded from fMRI

Source: https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.adw1464

In six participants, a language-model pipeline translated fMRI responses to viewed videos into descriptions of their semantic content. Video identification reached about 50% among 100 candidates, compared with 1% chance. Results also extended to instructed video recall and persisted when the canonical language network was excluded, supporting a shared semantic representation beyond that network. The experiment used extensive participant-specific training; it was not unrestricted reading of private thoughts or a clinical aphasia trial.

Each run reads about 1,500 papers and executes 42,000 lines of analysis code; outside scientists judged 79.4% of its conclusions accurate. Of seven discoveries, three reproduce results already obtained by humans and four are new. ## AlphaFold modeling guides discovery of RPA as a human telomerase processivity factor
2025-10-30 · biology · University of Wisconsin-Madison
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-10-rpa-telomerase-processivity-alphafold.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1126/science.ads5297

RPA was identified as a telomerase processivity factor that stimulates telomerase in vitro. AlphaFold modeling predicted that RPA engages a telomerase surface distinct from the one bound by TPP1; guided by this, engineered TERT separation-of-function mutants lost RPA-mediated stimulation and showed impaired telomere elongation, and short-telomere disease-associated TERT mutations reduced RPA-dependent stimulation. AlphaFold served as a guide within extensive wet-lab experiments.

## Machine learning predicts timing and fault-state evolution in meter-scale laboratory earthquakes
2025-10-30 · physics · Kyoto University; Disaster Prevention Research Institute, Kyoto University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-10-machine-learning-predicts-timing-and-fault-state-evolution-in-meter-scale-laboratory-earthquakes.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-64542-4

A Random Forest using a network representation of acoustic-emission event catalogs predicted the timing of meter-scale laboratory mainshocks from tens of seconds to milliseconds ahead (test-set log R²=0.84). Feature analysis found systematic changes in event intervals and seismic moments as failure approached; comparison with dynamic simulations led the authors to infer that acoustic emissions indirectly encode stress evolution on creeping fault patches. This is a laboratory-scale result, not a validated method for forecasting natural earthquakes.

## A six-metabolite machine-learning panel and isovalerylcarnitine findings for gastric cancer
2025-10-27 · medicine · Zhejiang Cancer Hospital; and six collaborating clinical centers; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Zhejiang Chinese Medical University; Wenzhou Medical University; National Cancer Center/National Clinical Research Center for Cancer, China
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-10-a-six-metabolite-machine-learning-panel-and-isovalerylcarnitine-findings-for-gastric-cancer.html
Source: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1038/s44321-025-00325-0

In two multicenter cohorts totaling 597 people, LASSO feature selection and five machine-learning classifiers produced a six-metabolite plasma panel for gastric-cancer diagnosis, with AUCs of 0.947–0.982 in discovery and 0.920–0.951 in validation. The panel included isovalerylcarnitine (C5), which was lower in cancer plasma and paired tumor tissue; the paper further reported a Mendelian-randomization association and cell-assay evidence linking C5 treatment to reduced gastric-cancer cell migration and invasion through calpain-associated changes in VE-cadherin and MMP2.

Genentech and collaborators trained the deep-learning model GNEprop on high-throughput screening data and screened more than 1.4 billion synthetically accessible molecules. In follow-up experiments, 82 selected compounds showed antibacterial activity against the sensitized E. coli ΔtolC strain; the paper reports a 90-fold higher hit rate than the training screen and describes chemically diverse hits, some with activity beyond that strain and validated biological targets.

## AI-guided reactor design improves a specific continuous-flow cycloaddition

Reac-Discovery combines learned geometry screening with automated experimental optimization of continuous-flow catalytic reactors. The peer-reviewed article reports a Schoen_G structured reactor with space–time yield of 803 g L−1 h−1 for a specific CO₂–epichlorohydrin cycloaddition, compared with 412 in the study’s initial data set. The comparison is study-specific and restricted to the authors’ reactor conditions; it does not establish industrial scale or net carbon removal. The article was published online on 13 October 2025; an earlier preprint described the platform and reaction, so this record attributes the 803 result to the journal version.

## Active learning discovers three high-entropy thermoelectrics with zT above 2
2025-10-09 · materials · Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology; Seoul National University; Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science; Hanbat National University; Korea University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-10-active-learning-discovers-three-high-entropy-thermoelectrics-with-zt-above-2.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1002/adma.202515054

A Gaussian-process model and Bayesian active-learning loop used an average thermoelectric quality factor as a physics-informed descriptor to search a nine-element chalcogenide composition space of 16,206 candidates. Across six iterations, the team synthesized and measured 80 samples; three high-entropy chalcogenides reached peak zT values of about 2.1 at 573 K, 2.3 at 473 K and 2.1 at 723 K. ## Neural-network satellite soil-moisture data expose global hotspots and pathways of rainfall coupling

Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-63999-7

An information-flow analysis of daily observations found statistically significant local surface-soil-moisture effects on precipitation over about 15.7% of global land (60°S–60°N) in the boreal warm season, with eight regional hotspots. Sensible-heat mediation dominated most hotspots, while evapotranspiration mediation dominated two African hotspots; remote moisture availability and boundary-layer-height variability helped explain regional differences. The transformer–variational-autoencoder ProT-VAE generated synthetic enzyme sequences that were tested experimentally. ## Active learning identifies high-performing electrolyte solvents for anode-free lithium metal cells
2025-09-25 · materials · University of Chicago
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-09-active-learning-anode-free-electrolytes.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-63303-7

Researchers used sequential Bayesian experimental design with Bayesian model averaging to select electrolyte solvents for testing in Cu||LiFePO4 cells, feeding cycle-capacity results back into the model over seven campaigns. The study reports seven top-performing solvent electrolytes and says four distinct solvents rival state-of-the-art performance; three were previously unreported as electrolytes for anode-free cells. ## ML-guided optimization improves photochemical cysteine arylation

Source: https://www.cambridge.org/engage/chemrxiv/article-details/68cc1a7323be8e43d6f4b2fb

The ChemRxiv v1 reports a two-stage optimization for nickel-catalyzed photochemical cysteine arylation: an embedding-based ranker screens categorical reagent choices, followed by Bayesian optimization of continuous conditions. The journal version reports 88% yield for both optimized conditions; the preprint reports 89% for the shorter second condition. ## A latent-state model links acute psychedelic treatment to sensory-guided mouse decisions

Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.09.18.677110v1.full

A fitted generalized-linear-model hidden Markov model identified sensory-engaged and history-biased choice states in a mouse perceptual-decision task. Acute psilocybin or ketamine shifted occupancy toward sensory-engaged states while increasing response time and accuracy. First posted in September 2025 and published in Science Advances in November 2026, the work used different cohorts across analyses; the final drug comparisons included 42 psilocybin and 30 ketamine mice. State-performance relationships were checked within the study. The experiment does not establish independent replication, human therapeutic benefits or a uniquely causal interpretation of the inferred states.

## New families of unstable singularities in fluid equations
2025-09-18 · mathematics · Google DeepMind; Brown University, NYU, and Stanford
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-09-fluidodinamica-singolarita.html
Source: https://deepmind.google/blog/discovering-new-solutions-to-century-old-problems-in-fluid-dynamics/

Physics-informed neural networks trained to near machine precision revealed a new family of unstable singularities (blow-ups) in three fluid-dynamics equations, with a clear pattern between blow-up speed and instability order for the incompressible porous-medium and Boussinesq equations. Work with Brown, NYU, and Stanford: a step toward computer-assisted proofs, not a proof; the Navier–Stokes problem remains open.

Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-09-ai-assisted-transfer-matrix-analysis-yields-an-exact-solution-for-the-1d-frustrated-q-state-potts-model.html
Source: https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/y5vc-3t6q

The study exactly solves the one-dimensional J₁–J₂ q-state Potts model for arbitrary q by reducing its q²×q² transfer matrix to a 2×2 maximally symmetric subspace and mapping it to an effective q-state Potts model in a field. OpenAI’s o3-mini-high reasoning model helped derive the q=3 case; the author then generalized the result to arbitrary q and checked the formulas numerically. The solution nontrivially extends an older mapping known for q=2/Ising and yields q-dependent phase and residual-entropy behavior.

Source: https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2025GL116118

For the 2016–2017 central Italy sequence, a combination of machine-learning techniques resolved two seismicity volumes with distinct fault orientations and Gutenberg–Richter b-values. Each structure retained its own b-value through the sequence; the apparent rise before the Mw 6.5 Norcia earthquake emerged when both were combined as their relative activity changed, showing that spatial heterogeneity can create an apparent temporal b-value signal.

## Physics-informed generative learning yields experimentally verified single-phase B2 intermetallic alloys

## Symbolic-regression turbulence analysis separates transferable flow physics from dataset-specific closure terms
2025-08-10 · physics · Northwestern Polytechnical University; Pennsylvania State University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-08-symbolic-regression-turbulence-analysis-separates-transferable-flow-physics-from-dataset-specific-closure-terms.html
Source: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-fluid-mechanics/article/abs/dataenabled-discovery-of-specific-and-generalisable-turbulence-closures/4077B2AAC80E5386F5A941ED13FBB451

Using high-fidelity data for plane channels, zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers and adverse-pressure-gradient boundary layers, the authors used symbolic regression to decompose learned turbulence-closure corrections into inner-layer, outer-layer and pressure-gradient components. They report that retaining the generalisable inner-layer term and adding flow-specific corrections improved predictions on held-out boundary-layer and aerofoil configurations, including unseen geometries and Reynolds numbers, outperforming baseline RANS closures in a priori and a posteriori tests. The authors identify conflation of transferable and training-specific flow behavior as a source of poor model generalization in the tested setting.

Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.06670v1

Interpretable decision trees applied to Dedekind-zeta coefficients helped the authors identify patterns in Galois extensions of degrees 4, 6, 8, 9 and 10. They formulated and proved mathematical criteria, including a nonic result: for the stated class, a₁₀₀₀(K) ≤ 4.5 implies the extension is cyclic. This theorem is a specific result; dataset classification accuracy is not a universal guarantee, and the paper reports a counterexample to an apparently perfect classifier branch. The arXiv v1 of 2025-08-08 and the 2026 journal version are one study.

## LHCb makes the first high-significance observation of the rare Σ⁺ → pμ⁺μ⁻ decay
2025-07-29 · physics · LHCb Collaboration; CERN
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-07-lhcb-makes-the-first-high-significance-observation-of-the-rare-p-decay.html
Source: https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/r3v2-kmmp

Using 5.4 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton collision data collected in 2016–2018, LHCb observed 237 ± 16 Σ⁺ → pμ⁺μ⁻ decays and measured a branching fraction of (1.08 ± 0.17) × 10⁻⁸. The dimuon spectrum showed no evidence of resonant structures, and the results are compatible with Standard Model expectations. ## Machine learning identifies disordered twist-angle sequences with strongly reduced thermal conductivity in multilayer graphene
2025-06-23 · materials · Sun Yat-sen University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-06-machine-learning-identifies-disordered-twist-angle-sequences-with-strongly-reduced-thermal-conductivity-in-multilayer-graphene.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41524-025-01678-3

Bayesian optimization and a CNN, coupled to non-equilibrium molecular dynamics, selected two-angle disordered twisted multilayer graphene structures with substantially lower simulated cross-plane thermal conductivity than aligned and periodic stacks. The optimized 14-layer sequence reached 0.095 W m−1 K−1 versus 0.512 W m−1 K−1 in aligned graphene in the reported model; phonon participation ratios and dynamical structure factors support strong partial phonon localization.

## Active learning identifies 28 new DFT-validated pressure-induced phase transitions
2025-06-20 · materials · Purdue University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-06-active-learning-identifies-28-new-dft-validated-pressure-induced-phase-transitions.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41524-025-01682-7

Across 13 active-learning cycles, a graph neural network screened phase pairs for pressure-induced transitions and selected cases for density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations. DFT confirmed 28 previously unreported transformations; 14 high-pressure phases were dynamically stable at transition pressure, including 10 also predicted dynamically stable at zero pressure. The study also identifies a previously unrecorded dynamically stable monoclinic P2₁/c phase of Cr₂O₃.

## Skala: a deep-learning exchange-correlation functional
2025-06-18 · chemistry · Microsoft Research
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-06-skala.html
Source: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/breaking-bonds-breaking-ground-advancing-the-accuracy-of-computational-chemistry-with-deep-learning/

It comes close to the 1 kcal/mol threshold on the W4-17 benchmark (0.85 kcal/mol on the single-reference subset) and is competitive with leading hybrid functionals on GMTKN55 at lower cost. It was trained on about 150,000 high-accuracy energy differences, roughly 100 times the previous dataset size. Accuracy is shown only within the training data's chemical space; it was not yet public at the time.

## Random forests identify surface geometry relationships associated with reduced bacterial attachment
2025-06-18 · materials · University of Nottingham; Maastricht University; Eindhoven University of Technology; La Trobe University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-06-random-forest-surface-attachment-design-rules.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60567-x

A screen of 2176 polymer surface patterns supplied measurements for random-forest models linking geometry to bacterial attachment. Held-out topographies supported predictive associations between attachment and surface coverage, feature size and spacing; the models outperformed a simpler roughness descriptor. The anti-attachment hits themselves came from experimental screening, not AI selection. The represented result is a learned structure–response relationship, without attributing the separate biological mechanism or animal findings to AI.

## Instantaneous voice-synthesis neuroprosthesis for a man with ALS
2025-06-12 · medicine · UC Davis; Stanford University; BrainGate consortium
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-06-instantaneous-voice-bci.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09127-3

A brain-computer interface decoding 256 microelectrodes in the ventral precentral gyrus synthesized the participant's intended voice causally, with a reported latency of about 10 ms per decoding step. Listeners understood almost 60% of synthesized words, compared with 4% when he was not using the device, and he could modulate intonation and sing short melodies. Caveat: a single participant with ALS, within the BrainGate2 trial, and the authors describe the technology as early stage.

## FerroAI guides discovery of a ferroelectric composition with high dielectric response

Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-06-ferroai-ferroelectric-morphotropic-boundary.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41524-025-01778-0

FerroAI, trained on text-mined phase-transition data, predicted composition–temperature phase behavior and a morphotropic phase boundary in a Zr/Hf co-doped barium titanate–BCT system. Researchers synthesized and characterized compositions near the predicted boundary. The x = 0.3 sample showed dielectric constant 9,535 at 1 kHz and 11,051 at 100 Hz at the transition temperature. The frequency-specific measured values should not be interchanged.

2025-06-10 · chemistry · Indian Institute of Technology Bombay; Scripps Research

A transfer-learned chemical language model generated novel chiral amino-acid ligands for palladium-catalyzed asymmetric β-C(sp³)–H activation, while an ensemble of 30 fine-tuned deep-learning regressors predicted reaction enantioselectivity. ## Topological learning and simulations predict lithium superionic-conductor candidates

A multiscale topological-learning workflow combined algebraic-topology descriptors, unsupervised clustering and ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations to screen lithium-containing structures. The study reports 14 candidate conductors meeting computational thresholds for diffusion barriers and electrochemical stability. ## Generative machine learning guides experimental synthesis of LiZn₂Pt and NiPt₂Ga Heusler phases
2025-06-05 · materials · Johns Hopkins University; Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory; Gdansk University of Technology
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-06-generative-machine-learning-guides-experimental-synthesis-of-lizn2pt-and-nipt2ga-heusler-phases.html
Source: https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2025/ra/d5ra00427f

Researchers combined a generative probabilistic crystal-graph model (PGCGM) with an ALIGNN stability predictor to propose and screen ternary structures, then used the model outputs to guide synthesis. They experimentally synthesized phase-pure LiZn₂Pt and NiPt₂Ga; the measured NiPt₂Ga adopts a tetragonal Heusler structure rather than the model’s cubic proposal, with DFT comparisons supporting its lower energy. This is one paper-level AI-enabled synthesis workflow and three related compounds, not three separate records.

CSF proteomics in 3,397 individuals from six prospective Alzheimer's disease cohorts found synapse proteins to be the strongest correlates of cognitive impairment, independent of amyloid and tau. ## Machine-learning workflow guides Na-doped RuO2 for durable acidic water electrolysis
2025-02-28 · chemistry · East China University of Science and Technology
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-02-ruo2-doping-rule-acidic-water-electrolysis.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.4c18300

An adaptive machine-learning workflow described potential-dependent evolution of the RuO2(110) surface, identifying an active state with distorted RuO5 units that converts to inert RuO4 units at higher potential. It yielded an inverse volcano-type doping rule, in which the dopant-oxygen bond strength should differ markedly from Ru-O. Applying the rule, the authors predicted and experimentally confirmed that Na stabilizes RuO2 in its active state: Na-RuO2 operated for over 1800 h in acidic oxygen evolution without degradation and showed durability in PEM electrolysis. Only one dopant is reported as confirmed in the abstract.

## CorrDiff: kilometer-scale weather forecasts with generative AI
2025-02-24 · climate · NVIDIA
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-02-corrdiff.html
Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/earth-2-ai-high-resolution-forecasts/

A diffusion model takes atmospheric data from 25-kilometer to 2-kilometer scale and also predicts variables absent from the inputs, such as radar reflectivity. The paper appeared the same day in Communications Earth and Environment; the initial model was tuned on Taiwan data with the Central Weather Administration, and Taiwan's disaster-reduction center uses it for alerts. ## Prospective Swedish cohort validates multimodal AI prostate-biopsy biomarker for recurrence and adverse pathology after prostatectomy
2025-02-21 · medicine · Skåne University Hospital; Lund University; Artera Inc.; University of California, San Francisco
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-02-prospective-swedish-cohort-validates-multimodal-ai-prostate-biopsy-biomarker-for-recurrence-and-adverse-pathology-after-prostatectomy.html
Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11995000/

A previously developed multimodal AI score was retrospectively applied to archived diagnostic biopsies and follow-up from a prospectively collected Swedish prostatectomy cohort. The score, derived from digitized diagnostic prostate-biopsy images plus age, PSA and clinical T-stage, was associated with post-surgical biochemical recurrence and adverse pathology. Among 143 men with evaluable data and median 8.8-year follow-up, the continuous score was associated with recurrence (subdistribution HR 2.45, 95% CI 1.77–3.38); among 88 evaluable for adverse pathology, OR was 4.85 (95% CI 2.54–10.78). Estimated 5-year recurrence was 25% in intermediate/high score versus 4% in low score.

## Mal-ID maps disease-associated immune-receptor patterns across infections and autoimmune conditions
2025-02-21 · medicine · Stanford University; Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation, Duke University, University of Pennsylvania and collaborating institutions
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-02-mal-id-maps-disease-associated-immune-receptor-patterns-across-infections-and-autoimmune-conditions.html
Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39977494/

Mal-ID analyzed B-cell and T-cell receptor repertoires from 593 people, including patients with COVID-19, HIV, systemic lupus erythematosus and type-1 diabetes, influenza-vaccination recipients and healthy controls. Its combined models classified held-out immune states and highlighted disease-associated receptor patterns; interpretation identified distinct autoreactivity features in lupus and type-1 diabetes and antigen-associated receptor sequences in COVID-19. The authors also evaluated classification on independent COVID-19 cohorts.

An autoencoder and deep embedded clustering surfaced low-frequency tremor-like episodes in seismic records preceding the 2023 Türkiye earthquake. An open-source model that generates thousands of protein structures per hour on a GPU and reproduces the equilibrium distribution of a molecular-dynamics simulation using 10,000 to 100,000 times fewer GPU-hours. Trained on more than 9.3 trillion nucleotides from over 128,000 genomes, it reads sequences up to 1 million nucleotides, flags harmful mutations, and designs genetic elements and genomes as long as those of simple bacteria. Source: https://ai.meta.com/blog/brain-ai-research-human-communication

A deep-learning decoder translated non-invasive EEG and MEG signals recorded during typing into sentence characters in an offline demonstration with 35 healthy volunteers. Mean character error rates were 67% for EEG and 32% for MEG, with a best MEG result of 19%. Researchers combined transcriptomic profiles with single-cell mechanical measurements from mouse and human systems and used machine-learning-based discriminative network analysis to infer a conserved five-gene module associated with cell mechanical properties. Five convolutional models ranked Euclid early-release images, followed by human visual grading. Spectroscopy and lens modeling support EUCL J081705.61+702348.8 as a strong lens, with foreground redshift 0.335 and lensed source redshift 1.475. Automatic differentiation optimized partial-differential-equation coefficients to increase the number of conserved quantities. Radio U-Net prompted reanalysis of LOFAR, XMM-Newton, DESI optical/near-infrared and weak-lensing data around cluster PSZ2 G083.29−31.03. ## AI-built Baihetan reservoir catalog reveals fault-controlled and depth-dependent seismicity
2025-02-06 · physics · China Earthquake Administration; Institute of Geophysics; Institute of Earthquake Forecasting

Source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0040195124004037

LOC-FLOW analysis of 55 stations and continuous waveforms from January 2021 to July 2022 identified 53,838 events around China’s Baihetan Reservoir, about four times the manual catalog, with reported relative location errors of tens of metres and recall of about 99% of manual events. The authors infer that post-impoundment seismicity is concentrated along regional structures and fractures, differs across the Jinsha River, and includes migration away from the inundation zone and with depth. They report depth-dependent b-value and water-depth/event-rate patterns consistent with different shallow and deep controls.

Transfer-learning transformer ensembles applied to deeper Hyper Suprime-Cam images of the Abell 194 cluster contributed to a vetted sample of 171 low-surface-brightness galaxies, including 87 reported as new discoveries. CHANCE, a supervised machine-learning model integrating patient-specific coding and non-coding mutations with drug and protein-interaction information, screened 5,197 TCGA/ICGC tumors against 923 FDA-approved non-oncology drugs. ## Multilingual model representations predict shared brain responses across languages

Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.02.01.636044v2

Multilingual neural-language-model embeddings enabled ridge-regression models of fMRI language-network responses that transferred to held-out languages across a 21-language study. The study combined existing data in 12 languages with newly collected data in nine more, supporting a shared representational component related to meaning. ## Leveraging machine learning to uncover multi-pathogen infection dynamics across co-distributed frog families
2025-01-29 · biology · Museum of Southwestern Biology, Department of Biology, University of New Mexico, Albuquerque, New Mexico, United States; Department of Biology, University of Central Florida, Orlando, Florida, United States
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-01-7717-peerj-18901.html
Source: https://peerj.com/articles/18901/

Among 1,281 sampled frogs, about 20% had at least one pathogen detected. Ranidae accounted for 74.3% of infections and had higher Bd intensity than the other two families. ## EvoGradient evolves antimicrobial peptides active against resistant pathogens
2025-01-17 · biology · Southeast University

Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41564-024-01907-3

EvoGradient uses an explainable deep-learning potency model and virtual sequence evolution to optimize candidate antimicrobial peptides. Applied to peptides encoded by low-abundance human oral bacteria, it virtually evolved 32 candidates; the six most effective were synthesized and tested against multidrug-resistant pathogens. The authors report activity across carbapenem-resistant E. coli, K. pneumoniae and A. baumannii and vancomycin-resistant E. faecium; pep-19-mod reduced bacterial loads by more than 95% in mouse thigh-infection models under the reported systemic and local administrations. A diffusion model trained on 608,000 stable materials. Compound TaCr2O6, generated with a constraint of 200 GPa bulk modulus, was synthesized and measured at 169 GPa (relative error under 20%), but with Ta–Cr disorder differing from the proposed structure. One experimental example.

## Active learning identifies a protoglobin variant with 99% yield and cis-selective cyclopropanation
2025-01-16 · biology · California Institute of Technology; University of California, Berkeley; Elegen Corp

Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11739421/

An iterative machine-learning campaign engineered the protoglobin from Pyrobaculum arsenaticum (ParPgb) for non-native cyclopropanation of 4-vinylanisole. After two model-guided rounds following an initial library screen, variant MPFDY gave 99% total cyclopropane yield and a 14:1 cis:trans ratio in the reported assay, compared with a parent variant that produced about 40% yield and favored trans product. ## Active learning guides experimental design of lead-free solder alloys

Uncertainty-aware Gaussian-process models and multi-objective Bayesian acquisition guided seven design–experiment iterations. The study reports two selected alloys, Si-4 and Se-5, tested for tensile strength and fracture elongation. Reported averages follow the authors’ stated one-sigma selection of repeated tensile tests. ## Machine-learning selection and Gaia astrometry confirm a 62-Jupiter-mass brown dwarf orbiting G 15-6
2025-01-08 · astronomy · European Space Agency (ESA), European Space Astronomy Centre
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2025-01-machine-learning-selection-and-gaia-astrometry-confirm-a-62-jupiter-mass-brown-dwarf-orbiting-g-15-6.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.09350

A machine-learning search of Gaia DR3 two-body astrometric orbits flagged G 15-6 as a likely low-mass companion system. Combining Gaia’s astrometric orbit with archival radial-velocity measurements resolved the inclination ambiguity and yielded a companion mass of 62.43 (+6.16/−5.44) Jupiter masses, firmly in the brown-dwarf range. The authors identify it as the first independently validated brown-dwarf companion selected by their ML method. The radial-velocity data predate the study; the new result is the Gaia orbit and AI-guided identification that resolve the companion mass, not a newly observed companion in 2025.

The General Expression Transformer (GET) model inferred cell-type-specific transcription-factor motif interactions from regulatory data and nominated a lymphocyte-specific interaction between PAX5 and nuclear-receptor-family factors. ## OmniFold enables an unbinned 24-dimensional Z+jets cross-section measurement by ATLAS
2024-12-30 · physics · ATLAS Collaboration; CERN Large Hadron Collider
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-12-omnifold-enables-an-unbinned-24-dimensional-z-jets-cross-section-measurement-by-atlas.html
Source: https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.133.261803

Using 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton data, ATLAS simultaneously unfolded 24 correlated Z+jets kinematic observables with the machine-learning method OmniFold and released the particle-level result as an unbinned event dataset. The measured total fiducial cross section is 1,808 ± 42 fb; most illustrative differential bins have 3–5% total uncertainty, rising to about 15% in tails. The measurement is more precise than the compared predictions for many distributions, especially Sherpa. The event-level release also supports derived observables, including an infrared-and-collinear-safe τ₂₁ measurement in a specified fiducial region.

The PICNIC gradient-boosting model ranked proteins for membership in biomolecular condensates using sequence-pattern and AlphaFold2-derived structural features. ## PlantRNA-FM identifies translation-associated RNA motifs and structure motifs in plants

Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11652376/

The PlantRNA-FM model, pretrained on sequence and predicted RNA structure from 1,124 plant transcriptomes, identified 5′-UTR motifs associated with translation efficiency across plant transcriptomes. Reporter assays in plants tested selected predictions: mutating a high-translation-associated RNA secondary-structure motif reduced measured translation efficiency by up to 5.3-fold, while disrupting a model-prioritized low-translation-associated RNA G-quadruplex motif increased it by up to 5.8-fold. A random-forest classifier trained on global basalt trace-element data distinguished destructive from constructive plate-boundary signatures, with the paper reporting greater than 98% accuracy on its labeled evaluation set. ## Machine learning-designed TADF molecules synthesized and characterized

Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-11-machine-learning-designed-tadf-molecules.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heliyon.2024.e40750

Two molecules chosen from 19 screened ML-designed thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) candidates were synthesized by palladium-catalyzed coupling and showed delayed fluorescence; photoluminescence quantum yield was 9.9% (mol_12, chloroform) and 19.8% (mol_16, toluene), with a singlet-triplet gap of 0.0084 eV for mol_12. The ML design model comes from the authors' earlier work; quantum yields are modest, measurements are in solution only, and only two molecules were made.

## Multi-agent reinforcement learning discovers a dominant iterated-game strategy
2024-11-26 · computer science · Shanghai Jiao Tong University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-11-multi-agent-rl-iterated-game-strategy.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-5462150/v1

Multi-agent reinforcement learning was used to explore strategy space beyond classic iterated-game strategies such as tit-for-tat, generous tit-for-tat, win-stay-lose-shift and zero-determinant strategies. It yielded a memory-two bilateral reciprocity (MTBR) strategy that outperforms a wide range of strategies in pairwise interactions with high payoffs. In evolving populations MTBR is reported to dominate and to foster higher cooperation and social welfare in homogeneous and heterogeneous structures and across game types, verified by simulations and mathematical analysis. The result is theoretical and simulated, with no empirical human data.

## Deep learning resolves subtle seismic-wave changes across the 2016 Norcia earthquake cycle
2024-11-20 · physics · Sapienza University of Rome; Pennsylvania State University

Source: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/alphaqubit-quantum-error-correction/

A Transformer-based decoder trained on data from a 49-qubit Sycamore processor made 6% fewer errors than tensor-network methods and 30% fewer than correlated matching in the largest experiments. It is too slow for real-time error correction on fast superconducting processors.

## OCx24: experimental catalysts for evaluating prediction models

## Generative agents built from interview transcripts simulate 1,000 people

LLM agents built from participants' full interview transcripts reproduced their General Social Survey answers at about 85% of the rate at which participants reproduced their own answers two weeks later, a normalized score. ## HiDDEN finds malignant-like cell signals in early multiple-myeloma precursor samples
2024-11-02 · biology · Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; collaborating institutions
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-11-hidden-finds-malignant-like-cell-signals-in-early-multiple-myeloma-precursor-samples.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-53666-8.pdf

HiDDEN refines sample-level case labels at single-cell resolution. In human bone-marrow single-cell RNA-seq data, its labels tracked manual neoplastic-cell annotations in mixed precursor samples and inferred malignant-like cells in three low-purity MGUS samples that the original manual analysis had labeled as containing only healthy cells. The inferred cells were enriched for previously described malignancy-associated gene signatures. In a separate mouse demyelination dataset, HiDDEN identified an early endothelial subpopulation with expression changes associated with angiogenesis, blood–brain-barrier breakdown and extracellular-matrix responses.

## PatternBoost: constructions in mathematics with a little help from AI
2024-11-01 · mathematics · Meta AI; University of Wisconsin-Madison; Google DeepMind; University of Sydney
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-11-patternboost-constructions.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00566

PatternBoost alternates a local search that generates candidate constructions with a transformer trained on the best ones. The authors report the best known solutions to several extremal combinatorics problems, including a counterexample to a conjecture that had been open for 30 years. Candidates are scored mechanically, so each construction is checked by computer; the abstract does not name the conjecture and the paper was not peer-reviewed at the time of posting.

A DenseNet-121 analyzed abdominal X-rays against recorded colorectal-cancer labels in Taiwanese hospital data. ## Iterative Gaussian process screening discovers selective aurein-derived antifungal peptides

## PICS-assisted survey reported seven new Large Magellanic Cloud pulsars
2024-08-09 · astronomy · University of Cape Town
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-08-pics-assisted-lmc-pulsar-survey.html
Source: https://academic.oup.com/mnras/article/533/3/2570/7731149

A MeerKAT survey of its first four Large Magellanic Cloud pointings reported seven new radio pulsars. The search pipeline applied the Pulsar Image-based Classification System (PICS), a deep-neural image classifier, to folded candidates and retained candidates above a PICS score threshold before human visual classification. The AI narrowed the candidate set (PICS score above 0.1, folded S/N above 7, DM above 3); the survey team then classified the remaining candidates manually and refolded neighbouring beams, and follow-up observations supplied additional checks. Six pulsars were detected again in follow-up; the incoherent-beam pulsar was not. A later paper reports 12 discoveries from additional pointings and timing follow-up of some Paper I pulsars, which are not additional discoveries in this entry.

## Machine learning identifies plasma protein signatures that predict onset of common and rare diseases

Researchers used regularized machine-learning models to select sparse plasma-protein signatures for 10-year incidence across 218 diseases in 41,931 UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project participants. ## PhaseNet-TF expands Tonga earthquake catalog and resolves the intermediate-depth double seismic zone
2024-06-06 · physics · Michigan State University; Stanford University; University of California, Berkeley

Source: https://academic.oup.com/gji/article/238/2/1073/7689220

A semi-supervised PhaseNet-TF workflow detected and relocated 13,616 events from a one-year Tonga OBS and land-station record, about 11 times the manually picked reference catalog. The denser catalog delineates the intermediate-depth double seismic zone to about 300 km and indicates that its lower plane is limited to roughly 19°–21°S, rather than continuous along the studied section. ## Towards a machine-learning assisted non-invasive classification of dengue severity using wearable PPG data: a prospective clinical study.

Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11167237/

Random forest, MLP/SVM and time-frequency CNN models classify dengue severity from wearable continuous PPG segments; five-fold cross-validation evaluates models. Prospective Vietnamese clinical dataset: 132 adults recruited, 127 after signal-quality filtering (1,223 hours), and 15 children in secondary acute-vs-follow-up analysis. The reviewed source supports this bounded result; external generalization, causal effects, and sustained operational impact remain unestablished where the source reports retrospective or internal evaluation.

## Active learning identifies a higher-activity streptavidin variant for gold-catalyzed hydroamination
2024-05-22 · biology · ETH Zurich; University of Basel and University of Regensburg

Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11273458/

An iterative active-learning campaign engineered a streptavidin artificial metalloenzyme for the known-to-the-authors gold-catalyzed hydroamination of 2-ethynylaniline to indole. Gaussian-process models guided screening across five residues in a 3.2-million-variant sequence space. The final-round library contained 38% variants more active than the prior reference, compared with 3% in the initial library. ## PICS-assisted survey reported seven new Small Magellanic Cloud pulsars
2024-05-21 · astronomy · The University of Manchester; Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy; South African Radio Astronomy Observatory; INAF-Osservatorio Astronomico di Cagliari; University of Cape Town; Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics; Leibniz University Hannover; Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics; Western Sydney University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-05-pics-assisted-smc-pulsar-survey.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12029

A MeerKAT survey of the Small Magellanic Cloud reported seven new radio pulsars. Each pointing produced hundreds of thousands of folded candidates, too many to inspect by eye. The pipeline partially classified them with PICS, a machine-learning system; a minimum PICS score of 10 per cent and a folded S/N of 7 reduced them to the order of a thousand per pointing, which researchers on the paper then classified by eye before follow-up. The paper does not identify each pulsar’s PICS score, so this is an AI-assisted survey-level result rather than a claim that the model independently discovered all seven sources. The paper also reports pulsar–nebula associations; the later timing paper follows this cohort and is not counted again.

A human-supervised self-driving laboratory selected and physically tested more than 25,000 additively manufactured polymer shell designs across an 11-dimensional parameter space. The campaign found a structure with 75.2% energy-absorbing efficiency, exceeding the paper’s previously reported maximum of 71.8% for balsa wood, and the authors derived transferable design heuristics from the resulting dataset. ## Machine learning predicts inadequate urate response to low-dose febuxostat in gout

Data from 340 male gout patients (an observational cohort and two clinical trials) receiving febuxostat 20 mg/day for at least 3 months were pooled; 68.9% and 51.8% were non-responders in short- and mid-term follow-up. A structure-based iterative-learning workflow combined prior α-synuclein fibril-binding hits, a junction-tree variational autoencoder, a random-forest regressor and Gaussian-process residual model to rank compounds for repeated testing. ## Structure-based virtual screening identifies mammalian enzymes catalyzing the second step of carnitine biosynthesis

## Machine learning reveals tropical aerosol-driven cloud expansion despite stronger rainfall
2024-04-11 · climate · University of Exeter; Met Office; ETH Zurich; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; University of Cambridge; University of Leeds; University of Reading
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-04-machine-learning-reveals-tropical-aerosol-driven-cloud-expansion-despite-stronger-rainfall.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41561-024-01427-z

Using satellite observations of four Kīlauea volcanic outgassing episodes in 2008 and 2018, an ML counterfactual analysis found that volcanic aerosols increased cloud cover and reflected sunlight over tropical marine shallow-convective clouds, even as rainfall strengthened. Cloud-cover adjustment contributed about 65% of aerosol–cloud cooling under mixed meteorological conditions and 84–87% in humid conditions; under humid, stable conditions, a 30% increase in droplet number could correspond to up to a 50% relative increase in cloud cover. The result identifies a tropical regime in which aerosol cloud expansion is strong and its response varies with humidity and stability.

## AI-assisted seismic catalog links the 2018 Baige landslide-dammed lakes to increased local earthquakes
2024-04-08 · physics · The Chinese University of Hong Kong; WSL Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research; Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Sichuan Earthquake Administration; Géoazur
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-04-ai-assisted-seismic-catalog-links-the-2018-baige-landslide-dammed-lakes-to-increased-local-earthquakes.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-47130-w

An earthquake catalog built with the PhaseNet machine-learning phase detector and cross-correlation/template matching revealed a statistically significant (over 99%) increase in small earthquakes as the second Baige landslide-dammed lake approached peak water level; rates returned toward background after breach. Coulomb-stress modeling found about 90% of the earthquakes in regions of positive modeled stress change, supporting likely triggering through direct water loading and pore-pressure diffusion. The paper presents this as evidence that earthquake–surface-hazard triggering can be bidirectional.

## Progeni predicts candidate melanoma and colorectal-cancer targets validated in cell models
2024-04-05 · biology · Tsinghua University; Westlake University; Jilin University; Silexon AI Technology
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-04-progeni-predicts-candidate-melanoma-and-colorectal-cancer-targets-validated-in-cell-models.html
Source: https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011945

Progeni combines a probabilistic knowledge graph with graph neural networks to rank disease-associated molecular targets. The authors selected six candidates lacking literature support and reported that knockdown of HSP90AB1 and MME reduced proliferation in a murine melanoma line, while knockdown of ADCY5, ADRA2A and EEF2 reduced proliferation in a murine colorectal-cancer line.

A generative model and protein-language-model-based temperature selector were combined in an iterative design procedure. ## Tree-based machine learning nominates Parabacteroides merdae and N-acetyl-D-mannosamine as ulcerative-colitis alleviators in a mouse model
2024-04-02 · biology · Jiangnan University; Wuxi Translational Medicine Research Center; Jiangsu Translational Medicine Research Institute Wuxi Branch; Wuxi People’s Hospital
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-04-tree-based-machine-learning-nominates-parabacteroides-merdae-and-n-acetyl-d-mannosamine-as-ulcerative-colitis-alleviators-in-a-mouse-model.html
Source: https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/19490976.2024.2336877

The researchers combined personalized gut-microbiome community metabolic models from human iHMP data with tree-based machine-learning feature selection to identify microbial strains and metabolites associated with ulcerative-colitis samples. Parabacteroides merdae ATCC 43,184 and N-acetyl-D-mannosamine were among the most predictive features; the strain was also the main modeled microbial contributor to the metabolite. In a DSS-induced mouse colitis experiment, oral administration of the bacterium or metabolite improved reported colitis measures.

## Spectroscopy validates machine-selected populations of obscured active galaxies
2024-04-01 · astronomy · University of Arizona; Princeton University; MMT Observatory
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-04-spectroscopy-validates-machine-selected-populations-of-obscured-active-galaxies.html
Source: https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.3847/1538-3881/ad28b4

Using a sample selected by unsupervised machine learning on optical and mid-infrared photometry, the team obtained 178 MMT spectra and found the brighter class was 85% Type I active galactic nuclei (AGN), with <3% non-AGN contamination, while a fainter class was 65% Type II AGN with 15% contamination, mainly star-forming galaxies. The follow-up showed that the machine-selected classes recover redder and more obscured AGN populations than typical optical spectroscopic samples.

## LAISS-assisted review reclassifies anomalous ZTF transients
2024-04-01 · astronomy · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; Pacific Northwest National Laboratory
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-04-laiss-assisted-review-reclassifies-anomalous-ztf-transients.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01235v1

Expert review of 455 previously observed transients changed 16 normal labels to anomalous; the random-forest model flagged 11 of these. Spectra, light curves and host context supported the reclassifications. This is a retrospective study-level result rather than a count of newly observed events or newly established physical classes. Human review and similarity searches also contributed, so the entire retrospective sample is not attributed to the classifier.
