## Deep-learning-guided electrochemistry identifies a mechanistic outlier in cobalt–organohalide reactions
2024-03-30 · chemistry · University of California, Los Angeles; University of Illinois Urbana–Champaign; University of Utah; Université Grenoble Alpes
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-03-autonomous-electrochemistry-mechanistic-outlier.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-47210-x

A UCLA-led team combined a ResNet voltammogram classifier with Bayesian experiment selection to investigate cobalt tetraphenylporphyrin reactions. The workflow flagged 4-chlorobutyronitrile as departing from the expected electron-transfer–chemical-reaction mechanism; additional manual measurements confirmed the anomaly. An alternative radical pathway remains a hypothesis. This is a laboratory proof of concept, not a general-purpose mechanistic oracle. The date records the journal version.

## SEEDS: weather ensembles generated with a diffusion model
2024-03-29 · climate · Google Research
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-03-seeds.html
Source: https://research.google/blog/generative-ai-to-quantify-uncertainty-in-weather-forecasting/

The model produces 256 members at 2° resolution every three minutes on a TPU and matches or exceeds the operational GEFS ensemble (31 members) on rank histograms, RMSE and CRPS. For the Lisbon heatwave (July 2022), with 16,384 members, none of GEFS’s 31 members was as warm as observed. One extreme case; depends on physics-based forecasts as seeds; published in Science Advances.

## Deep-learning-enhanced Sparta earthquake catalog resolves a shallow multifault rupture
2024-03-29 · physics · Georgia Institute of Technology; University of Science and Technology of China; North Carolina State University; Chinese Academy of Sciences
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-03-deep-learning-enhanced-sparta-earthquake-catalog-resolves-a-shallow-multifault-rupture.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-024-01316-8

For the 2020 Mw 5.1 Sparta, North Carolina sequence, an EQTransformer-based catalog combined with matched-filter detections and differential-time relocations contains 1,761 high-precision events, about 5.8 times the original NEIC count. ## Machine learning on genomes estimates country-level tuberculosis drug resistance profiles

Source: https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjgh-2023-013532

A validated random forest predicted phenotypic resistance to 12 drugs from whole-genome sequences of 19,149 Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from 29 countries, bias-corrected, to estimate country-level antibiograms; for example, global pooled isoniazid mono-resistance was 10.9%. ## Machine learning links circulating tyrosine and distinct lipid-metabolite features to diabetic kidney disease and retinopathy detection
2024-03-28 · medicine · Singapore Eye Research Institute; Singapore National Eye Centre; National University of Singapore; Duke-NUS Medical School
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-03-machine-learning-links-circulating-tyrosine-and-distinct-lipid-metabolite-features-to-diabetic-kidney-disease-and-retinopathy-detection.html
Source: https://www.jmir.org/2024/1/e41065/

In 2,772 adults with diabetes from Singapore’s population-based SEED study, LASSO and gradient-boosting models screened 220 circulating metabolites and 19 clinical factors for prevalent diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and retinopathy (DR), then were externally assessed in 5,843 UK Biobank participants. Both outcomes shared diabetes duration, insulin use, age and tyrosine as important model features. DKD additionally selected cardiovascular disease history, antihypertensive use, lactate, citrate and the intermediate-density-lipoprotein cholesterol-ester/total-lipid ratio; DR additionally selected HbA1c, glucose, pulse pressure and alanine. External AUCs were 0.791 for DKD and 0.778 for DR, versus 0.691 and 0.760 for conventional adjusted logistic-regression comparators.

## A biophysics-informed protein language model designs functional GFP variants
2024-03-17 · biology · University of Wisconsin-Madison
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-03-metl-gfp-protein-engineering.html
Source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.03.15.585128v1

Mutational Effect Transfer Learning (METL) combines transformer pretraining on simulated protein biophysics with fine-tuning on experimental sequence–function data. Using only 64 experimental GFP examples, the authors designed 20 previously untested variants and measured their fluorescence; 16 showed measurable fluorescence, although none was brighter than wild-type GFP. The result demonstrates functional design under a small-data setup, not improved brightness over wild type. The result was present in the bioRxiv version posted 2024-03-17; the GEM@ICLR 2024 workshop paper provides the detailed 20-variant assay report, and the later journal version is the same study.

## AI-assisted Hubble asteroid sample extends the shallow size-distribution slope to H≈20

Source: https://www.aanda.org/articles/aa/pdf/2024/03/aa46771-23.pdf

Using 632 serendipitously imaged Hubble Space Telescope asteroids found by the prior AI-assisted Hubble Asteroid Hunter survey, the authors fit trail parallax to estimate distances, absolute magnitudes, and approximate sizes. Their cumulative magnitude distribution has a shallower slope (α≈0.26) from H=15 to about H=20, extending the previously reported trend by roughly two magnitudes; the analyzed sample is dominated by potential main-belt objects smaller than 1 km.

MolE-XGBoost prioritized existing compounds. ## AI-ranked SARS-CoV-2 protein interactions guide discovery of an NSP10–NSP16 inhibitor

A machine-learning classifier applied to quantitative PPI assay data and AlphaFold-Multimer predictions to prioritize SARS-CoV-2 protein interactions; 15 of 34 high-confidence interactions were not previously listed in IMEx. Researchers developed MutComputeX, a structure-based residual neural network for assessing amino-acid substitutions in protein–ligand environments, and used it with a 4′-O-methylnorbelladine biosensor to engineer the plant methyltransferase Nb4OMT in Escherichia coli. An autonomous materials-discovery workflow used AI-feedback density-functional-theory simulations to select six previously well-explored ternary oxide systems for synthesis. In the Ca–Ru–O campaign, experiments yielded two previously unreported phases; room-temperature diffraction and follow-up characterization most clearly support an isolated low-temperature calcium-rich phase, approximately Ca1+xRuO3+y, distinct from conventional CaRuO3. ## An ML-generated MinE homolog restores bacterial cell division patterning in vivo

A machine-learning-generated MinE homolog, synMinEv25, restored Min oscillations and wild-type-like cell growth and morphology when substituted for the native minE gene in an E. coli strain lacking minDE. ## Gaussian-process-assisted engineering of a ketoreductase for an ipatasertib precursor
2024-02-28 · biology · Institute of Chemistry and Biotechnology, Zurich University of Applied Sciences; F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd.

Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10902378/

A six-round engineering campaign combined mutational scans, structure-guided libraries and Gaussian-process models. The model-aided library yielded M3, reported with 22-fold higher apparent activity than wild type in the UV assay. Three subsequent conventional mutagenesis rounds produced M6, a 10-substitution descendant with 64-fold higher apparent kcat, but also about 12-fold higher apparent KM; do not attribute M6 as a direct model output or treat kcat as production yield. These are process-relevant laboratory results, not a commercial production run or drug efficacy.

2024-02-09 · physics · Cornell University; Stanford University; Argonne National Laboratory; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2024-02-machine-learning-x-ray-analysis-provides-bulk-evidence-for-a-bragg-glass-phase-in-pdxerte3.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41567-023-02380-1

Researchers combined extensive X-ray diffraction with X-ray Temperature Clustering (X-TEC) to identify Bragg-glass signatures in the charge-density-wave material PdₓErTe₃. Their analysis extracted diffraction features across about 20,000 Brillouin zones and found a diverging correlation length and a phase diagram consistent with a Bragg-glass transition. The result provides bulk diffraction evidence for a phase that had been difficult to establish experimentally.

A deep-learning-based catalog pipeline processed 18 months of seismic-array data and located 1,891 shallow earthquakes, more than twice the 849 events in the prior manual catalog. Of 36 selected catalysts, 30 reached combined ethane and ethylene yields of at least 15% in the reported tests. This is a small-data, reaction-specific catalyst screening outcome; the paper also tests feature engineering on other catalysis datasets. A ChemRxiv version predates the journal publication, and this record does not claim journal-version priority.

In a proteomic study, researchers measured paired CSF and serum samples in a discovery cohort and used random-forest machine learning to select a 19-protein CSF panel and an eight-protein serum panel to distinguish mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer disease from cognitively normal participants. ## Deep clustering reveals weak tremor three days before the 2021 Geldingadalir eruption

Unsupervised deep clustering of historical seismic recordings revealed a weak tremor beginning around midday on 16 March 2021, roughly three days before the Geldingadalir eruption in Iceland. A machine-learning-guided high-throughput screen identified a five-component D-amino-acid mixture (“D-mix”) with about 78% anti-biofilm activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa at 100 μM. ## Machine-learning denoising exposes strong size scaling in deep-earthquake rupture parameters
2023-12-18 · physics · University of Washington, Department of Earth and Space Sciences
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2023-12-machine-learning-denoising-exposes-strong-size-scaling-in-deep-earthquake-rupture-parameters.html
Source: https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2023JB027334

A multitask neural denoiser recovered teleseismic P-wave pulses from deep Mw 5.0+ earthquakes that had previously been too noisy for source analysis. The study found moment–duration scaling M₀ ∼ τ⁴, stress-drop scaling Δσ ∼ M₀⁰·²¹ and radiated-energy scaling Eᵣ ∼ M₀¹·²⁴; deep events had a median radiation efficiency near 5%, weak directivity and few subevents. After accounting for rigidity, no systematic depth trend in duration, stress drop or radiated energy remained across 100–700 km.

A staged serum-proteomics study across 1,002 individuals used random-forest machine learning to select a four-marker panel, P4 (HABP2, CD163, AFP and PIVKA-II). ## AlphaZero finds improved finite extremal-graph bounds

A neural network-guided AlphaZero search with a curriculum generated triangle- and 4-cycle-free graphs that improve known lower bounds for the extremal function ex(n,{C3,C4}) over finite sizes; the proceedings report AlphaZero improvements for n=64–136 and release the graph constructions. StrokeClassifier is an ensemble meta-model of 9 machine learning classifiers applied to NLP-extracted features from discharge summaries of 2,039 non-cryptogenic ischemic stroke patients at 2 academic hospitals, predicting a 4-level etiology set by agreement of at least 2 vascular neurologists. ## CNN-assisted search confirms quadruply lensed quasar PS J2107−1611
2023-10-06 · astronomy · École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne; University of Liège; European Southern Observatory; Universidad Andrés Bello
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2023-10-cnn-assisted-search-confirms-quadruply-lensed-quasar-ps-j21071611.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04494

A convolutional neural network trained on simulated lens images screened 27,760 preselected quasar candidates with multiple nearby Pan-STARRS detections. Researchers visually inspected the top 2,000 scores and selected follow-up targets; spectroscopy and multi-survey imaging established PS J2107−1611 as a quadruply imaged quasar at redshift 2.673, with a 4.3-arcsecond image separation and a lensed host-galaxy arc. Its fold-image optical fluxes are roughly 15 times fainter than a smooth lens-mass model predicts, while radio flux ratios are consistent with that model. The date is the original preprint posting; the journal version appeared in November 2023.

## Unsupervised learning defines liver injury phenotypes in pulmonary hypertension

## Machine learning helps recover dimension from quantum periods for a class of Fano varieties

A feed-forward neural network classified the dimension of Fano varieties from quantum-period coefficients with 98% accuracy on the authors’ dataset. ## Deep learning detects an emerging anthropogenic warming fingerprint in daily precipitation

## Deep-learning knee imaging phenotypes reveal osteoarthritis genetic and fracture associations
2023-08-21 · biology · University of Texas at Austin; Dell Medical School; Columbia University; New York Genome Center

Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41746-023-00903-x

Using knee DXA scans from the UK Biobank, a ResNet-101 model identified 1,931 more probable knee-osteoarthritis cases than health-record coding and a U-Net segmentation model estimated minimum joint-space width (mJSW). In 29,257 participants, the quantitative mJSW phenotype had substantially higher SNP heritability than the binary phenotypes and yielded 18 genome-wide-significant loci, compared with one for the image-based binary classifier and six for ICD-10 coding; only one mJSW locus was already significant in a large prior knee-OA GWAS. A closed-loop error-correction learning workflow guided synthesis of PbSe alloyed with SnSb and documented a previously unexplored low-temperature thermoelectric family. In a prospective study of 1690 melanocytic lesions in 143 high-risk patients, 2D and 3D CNN risk scores were compared with dermatologists against histopathology. ## SIMMER-guided experiments identify gut bacterial strains that deplete methotrexate
2023-06-12 · biology · Gladstone Institutes; University of California, San Francisco; Chan Zuckerberg Biohub San Francisco
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2023-06-simmer-guided-experiments-identify-gut-bacterial-strains-that-deplete-methotrexate.html
Source: https://elifesciences.org/articles/82401

SIMMER combines reaction-chemistry and protein-sequence similarity to predict gut microbial species and enzymes responsible for drug biotransformations. For methotrexate (MTX), the model predicted candidate strains and enzyme sequences; researchers tested 42 gut bacterial isolates by HPLC. SIMMER predicted 13 isolates as MTX-metabolizing, and 10 of those tested isolates showed MTX depletion; the association was significant in the study (Fisher exact p=0.046). ## ATLAS graph neural network enables first observation of four-top-quark production
2023-06-12 · physics · ATLAS Collaboration; CERN
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2023-06-atlas-graph-neural-network-enables-first-observation-of-four-top-quark-production.html
Source: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1140/epjc/s10052-023-11573-0

Using 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton collisions, ATLAS observed simultaneous production of four top quarks in same-sign dilepton and multilepton events, with 6.1σ observed (4.3σ expected) significance. The measured cross-section is 22.5⁺⁶·⁶₋₅·₅ fb, consistent with the Standard Model prediction within 1.8σ. A graph neural network separated the four-top signal from dominant backgrounds in the signal extraction.

Machine-learning models learned relationships between crystallization composition/conditions and zeolite characteristics from prior synthesis records, guiding human selection of conditions for faujasite synthesis. ## Machine-learning microbiome score is associated with future Crohn's disease in relatives
2023-05-30 · medicine · Mount Sinai Hospital; University of Toronto
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2023-05-gut-microbiome-risk-score-crohns-relatives.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1053/j.gastro.2023.05.032

In a prospective cohort of 3483 healthy first-degree relatives of patients with Crohn's disease, machine learning on 16S rRNA gut microbiome composition defined a microbiome risk score (MRS). In an independent validation cohort the MRS gave a hazard ratio of 2.24 (95% CI 1.03-4.84, P = .04) and captured individuals who developed disease up to 5 years before onset (AUC > 0.65). The five most important taxa were Ruminococcus torques, Blautia, Colidextribacter, an uncultured Oscillospiraceae group and Roseburia. The effect is modest and the confidence interval wide; it shows association, not causation.

Source: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/epi.17629

At one specialized pediatric epilepsy center, an NLP support system using an SVM and n-gram features screened neurology notes and randomized providers of 284 identified potential candidates to receive an alert or usual care. During a median 24-month follow-up, presurgical evaluation referrals were 9.8% with alerts and 3.1% in controls (adjusted HR 3.21; 95% CI 0.95–10.8; one-sided p=.03); nine alert-group children and no controls underwent surgery. ## Machine-learning classification shows rigidity-corrected moment release is similar across earthquake depths
2023-05-01 · physics · University of Science and Technology of China; Mengcheng National Geophysical Observatory
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2023-05-machine-learning-classification-shows-rigidity-corrected-moment-release-is-similar-across-earthquake-depths.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41561-023-01176-5

Random-forest classification of source-time-function characteristics for 3,675 global Mw > 5.5 earthquakes showed that depth-dependent rigidity explains much of the differences in rupture duration, length and stress drop between shallow, intermediate and deep earthquakes. Once medium rigidity is corrected, the analyzed events exhibit similar moment-release processes, supporting a constant-strain-drop interpretation across depths and host-rock types.

## Machine learning finds ribbon-knot certificates and rules out candidate pairs

Bayesian optimization and reinforcement learning search for sequences of knot moves that certify a knot is ribbon. ## AI-generated catalyst design led to experimentally tested polymerization catalysts

Source: https://chemrxiv.org/engage/chemrxiv/article-details/63e668409da0bc6b33b1870c

A regression-transformer model fine-tuned on historical ring-opening-polymerization data generated candidate catalysts. Researchers selected synthetically accessible, modified surrogates of one model-generated catalyst for laboratory testing. One surrogate, 5c, reached 60% conversion in 32 minutes for monomer 2a and 100% conversion in 45 minutes for monomer 2d, with reported dispersities of 1.06 and 1.34, respectively. The first ChemRxiv v1 (2022-06-27) described computational generation and recovery of a literature-known catalyst. The experimental results appeared in ChemRxiv v2, posted 2023-02-13, and the 2023 peer-reviewed journal article followed on 2023-06-21. The measured tests concern modified surrogates, not the unmodified generated structure.

The CellOracle machine-learning workflow used single-cell gene-regulatory networks to prioritize transcription factors for perturbation in zebrafish development. An unsupervised repeating-signal detector, combined with template matching, exposed small earthquake bursts in a region of the Eagle Ford shale where conventional catalogs had detected little seismicity. ## Random forest and SVM identify sperm protein biomarkers of bull field fertility
2022-10-26 · biology · University College Dublin
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2022-10-bull-sperm-protein-fertility-biomarkers.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.3168/jds.2022-22273

Sperm proteomes (LC-MS) of 54 Irish Holstein bulls (23 low, 14 medium, 17 high fertility) and 18 Danish bulls (8 low, 10 high) were analyzed. A modified t-test selected 301 differentially abundant proteins and random forest selected 34 biomarker proteins. An SVM trained on the Irish bulls predicted fertility class of the Danish bulls with 94.4% accuracy, misclassifying only one high-fertility bull. The validation cohort is small and no functional wet-lab test is reported.

## Deep learning distinguishes eyes with prior optic neuritis on peripapillary OCT ring scans
2022-10-25 · medicine · Max Delbrück Center; Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin; Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2022-10-oct-deep-learning-prior-optic-neuritis.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1002/acn3.51632

A dilated residual convolutional neural network classified OCT peripapillary ring scans from healthy eyes (1033 scans) and eyes with prior optic neuritis (510 scans from 140 MS patients). The network reached accuracy 0.85 and AUC 0.86, against AUC 0.77 for retinal nerve fiber layer thickness alone. ## Deep-learning fiber-force microscopy reveals how cells pull on fibrous environments
2022-10-25 · biology · Virginia Tech
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2022-10-deep-learning-fiber-force-microscopy.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1101/2022.10.24.513423

Deep-learning-enabled live-cell fiber-force microscopy (DLFM) computes forces that cells exert on tissue-like fiber networks from phase microscopy, tracking cell movement and fiber deformation without fluorescent labels. It showed ten-fold changes in force as cells change shape during migration, force dipoles in cell-cell interactions, and altered force patterns during stem cell differentiation. Experiments and modelling indicate cells form force-generating adhesions throughout their body in fibrous environments. Preprint; the abstract gives few numbers beyond the ten-fold change.

## Robot-guided optimization identifies six non-aqueous electrolytes with improved fast-charge performance
2022-09-27 · materials · Carnegie Mellon University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2022-09-robot-guided-optimization-identifies-six-non-aqueous-electrolytes-with-improved-fast-charge-performance.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-32938-1

A closed-loop platform paired Clio, an automated electrolyte-formulation and conductivity-testing robot, with Dragonfly Bayesian optimization. In 42 experiments over two workdays, it selected six non-aqueous electrolyte formulations from a LiPF₆ and EC/EMC/DMC design space. The team tested these formulations in 220 mAh graphite‖NMC pouch cells; all showed improved fast-charging capability relative to a baseline electrolyte selected in advance from the same design space. ## ATLAS boosted decision trees enable first observation of triple-W boson production

In 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV LHC data, ATLAS observed simultaneous WWW production at 8.0σ (5.4σ expected) and measured an inclusive cross-section of 820 ± 100(stat) ± 80(syst) fb. ## X-ray machine-learning analysis reveals opposing Cd/Re displacements and Re 5d involvement in Cd₂Re₂O₇ structural order
2022-06-09 · materials · Cornell University; Argonne National Laboratory; University of Tennessee, Knoxville; University of Maryland; National Institute of Standards and Technology
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2022-06-x-ray-machine-learning-analysis-reveals-opposing-cd-re-displacements-and-re-5d-involvement-in-cd2re2o7-structural-order.html
Source: https://eunahkim.lassp.cornell.edu/sites/kim/files/publications/Harnessing%20interpretable%20and%20unsupervised%20machine%20learning%20to%20address%20big%20data%20from%20modern%20X-ray%20diffraction.pdf

Unsupervised X-ray diffraction temperature clustering (X-TEC) analyzed high-volume temperature-dependent diffraction data from Cd₂Re₂O₇. The extracted selection rules indicate that Cd and Re displacements are approximately equal in amplitude and opposite in phase, revealing a previously unrecognized involvement of Re 5d electrons in the structural order. The analysis also resolves X-ray diffraction evidence for fluctuations associated with the structural transitions. This is a data-driven interpretation of measured diffraction, not a new direct imaging of atom trajectories.

## ColabFold: free protein folding with AlphaFold2 or RoseTTAFold

Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2022-05-colabfold.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-022-01488-1

ColabFold pairs AlphaFold2 or RoseTTAFold with fast MMseqs2 homology search, running free on Google Colab. Beyond benchmark comparisons, the paper reports predicting structures for 1,762 Methanocaldococcus jannaschii proteins in 48 hours on one GPU and using predicted complexes to help determine the 120 MDa human nuclear-pore structure with cryo-electron microscopy. From 4695 pregnant volunteers in North Carolina and Zambia, blind ultrasound sweeps of the gravid abdomen were recorded alongside standard fetal biometry, and a neural network was trained to estimate gestational age. Performance appeared to extend to sweeps collected by untrained providers in Zambia with low-cost devices. The model was not tested in a clinical deployment.

A machine learning drug-screening model predicted the natural product ingenol as promoting megakaryocyte differentiation and platelet production. ## Cell2location: mapping fine-grained cell types in spatial transcriptomics
2022-01-13 · biology · Helmholtz Munich; Wellcome Sanger Institute
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2022-01-cell2location.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-021-01139-4

Cell2location is a Bayesian model that resolves fine-grained cell types in spatial transcriptomics data by accounting for technical variation and sharing information across locations. Applied to three tissues, it revealed regional astrocyte subtypes in mouse brain, a rare pre-germinal center B cell population in human lymph node, and fine immune populations in human gut lymphoid follicles. Caveat: the reported results are biological findings from the method's application, with no single quantitative accuracy figure confirmed in the abstract.

## Machine learning guides discovery of hard Fe–Nb–B metallic-glass films
2022-01-10 · materials · Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lightsource, SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory; Colorado School of Mines; National Renewable Energy Laboratory; Argonne National Laboratory; University of Maryland
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2022-01-ml-high-throughput-fe-nb-b-glass.html
Source: https://www.nrel.gov/docs/fy22osti/80853.pdf

Random-forest models for glass formation and hardness helped select Fe–Nb–B composition regions for sputtered-film experiments. The study reports a maximum measured hardness of 29 GPa for Fe₃Nb₂₅B₇₂ and an H/E ratio of 0.09 for Fe₂₀Nb₁₂B₆₈. H/E is used as an estimate of wear resistance, not a direct wear test. Samples were 500–800 nm films with substrate-effect corrections; bulk properties and industrial production were not demonstrated. This extends earlier machine-learning/high-throughput work on metallic glasses and is one study.

The MuMMI machine-learning multiscale simulation ensemble found that local membrane lipid fingerprints correlate with wild-type KRAS clustering and orientation, with many simulated RAS–RAS interfaces appearing nonspecific. Complementary liposome and diffusion experiments supported lipid-dependent RAS adhesion and dynamics, motivating the authors' conclusion that lipids can mediate RAS multimer organization.

## On-cell phage display with machine learning yields picomolar antibodies to Frizzled-7

## Neural network supports a six-gene predictor of infliximab failure in ulcerative colitis

Source: https://doi.org/10.3389/fimmu.2021.742080

Three GEO datasets were analyzed with the RobustRankAggreg algorithm to identify genes differing between infliximab responders and non-responders, and an artificial neural network was used to validate their predictive value. The six genes CDX2, CHP2, HSD11B2, RANK, NOX4 and VDR gave a repeated overall AUC of 0.850 ± 0.103, and 0.759 ± 0.065 in an independent GEO dataset. A machine learning model was developed on the Huawei Heart Study smart-device photoplethysmography data and optimized in 554 individuals with 469,267 PPG datasets. ## Deep learning measures the thoracic aorta in cardiac MRI to enable genetic analysis

Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-021-00962-4

A deep-learning model measured ascending and descending thoracic aortic dimensions in 4.6 million UK Biobank cardiac magnetic resonance images. Genome-wide association studies in 39,688 individuals identified 82 loci for ascending and 47 for descending aortic diameter (14 overlapping), and further analyses prioritized genes including SVIL. Two machine-learning-guided directed-evolution series for sortase A were run with and without the known high-activity 5M variant in the initial training set. The authors report new variants with higher activity than 5M in a GFP/YFP cross-linking assay. This is not a 2.2–2.5-fold improvement over wild type; the known 5M comparator is already engineered. Feature selection used ability to find 5M and may bias exploration. The related GB1 analysis uses an existing dataset, not a second laboratory discovery. Sequence-level comparison with later sortase work remains open.

## Machine-learning search surfaces extreme T-subdwarf candidate CWISE J0523
2021-11-16 · astronomy · Northern Arizona University; Caltech IPAC; Backyard Worlds: Planet 9; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-11-machine-learning-search-surfaces-extreme-t-subdwarf-candidate-cwise-j0523.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.08182v1

A machine-learning-assisted search of WISE time-series images helped identify the high-proper-motion object CWISE J052306.42-015355.4. Its colors suggest an extreme T-subdwarf candidate, while spectral classification, parallax, distance and metallicity remain uncertain. Human and citizen-science pathways also contributed. The candidate result was public in the November 2021 preprint before the January 2022 journal article.

## Neural-network-guided autonomous experiments reveal an unreported TosMIC reaction
2021-11-11 · chemistry · University of Glasgow School of Chemistry
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-11-neural-network-guided-autonomous-experiments-reveal-an-unreported-tosmic-reaction.html
Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34849401/

A reactivity-seeking neural network coupled to an autonomous reaction platform navigated unknown chemical mixtures using real-time analytical data. Among the reactions it identified, follow-up characterization revealed an unreported photochemical reaction and a new reactivity mode for p-toluenesulfonylmethyl isocyanide (TosMIC): six equivalents of TosMIC underwent a multistep single-substrate cascade yielding a trimeric product in 47% unoptimized yield and forming five C–C bonds.

## MutCompute guides thermostable Bst DNA polymerase variants
2021-11-11 · biology · The University of Texas at Austin
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-11-mutcompute-bst-polymerase-variants.html
Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9514386/

MutCompute predicted substitutions in Bst DNA polymerase; the authors constructed and tested variants in loop-mediated isothermal amplification assays. The Mut235 triple variant showed the highest activity among four tested triple-mutant variants and remained active at 73 °C; its reported melting temperature was 78.1 °C. The evidence is in vitro and does not establish clinical diagnostic performance. The journal article cites a bioRxiv v1 posted 2021-04-15, but that version’s full text was inaccessible in this review; this entry uses the verified journal result and does not claim when the Mut235 result first appeared.

## Deep learning extends the mapped extent of a North Anatolian Fault slow-slip event
2021-11-10 · physics · Los Alamos National Laboratory; École Normale Supérieure; University of California, Santa Cruz and collaborators
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-11-deep-learning-extends-the-mapped-extent-of-a-north-anatolian-fault-slow-slip-event.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.13849

A deep convolutional autoencoder trained on synthetic deformation and atmospheric-noise time series recovered millimeter-scale ground motion from real InSAR without being given the fault location. Applied to COSMO-SkyMed observations of the 2013 North Anatolian Fault slow-slip event, it detected about 2 mm of slip beyond the previously identified segment and revised the estimated along-strike event length from about 10 km to 15–20 km. The same paper used the approach to resolve transient millimeter-scale subsidence at California’s Coso geothermal field. This is one paper-level finding enabled by the model’s extraction of deformation signals from noisy satellite data.

## High-resolution machine-learning catalog outlines a potential unmapped fault in the Weiyuan shale-gas region
2021-11-01 · physics · The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Sichuan Earthquake Agency
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-11-high-resolution-machine-learning-catalog-outlines-a-potential-unmapped-fault-in-the-weiyuan-shale-gas-region.html
Source: https://eppcgs.org/article/doi/10.26464/epp2021055?viewType=HTML

A machine-learning event detector combined with waveform cross-correlation produced a high-resolution catalog for injection-induced seismicity in the Weiyuan area, identifying one-third more earthquakes than the routine catalog and improving magnitude completeness. Spatial migration patterns show a pore-pressure diffusion front; a cluster outlines a potential unmapped fault that may have hosted the region’s largest recorded event, the September 2019 Mw 5.2 earthquake.

## AlphaFold model of full-length honey bee vitellogenin restrained by electron microscopy
2021-10-31 · biology · Norwegian University of Life Sciences
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-10-honey-bee-vitellogenin-structure-prediction.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1002/2211-5463.13316

Researchers modeled full-length honey bee vitellogenin using homology modeling and AlphaFold, then used a negative-stain electron microscopy map to restrain, orient and validate the model. The model identified a highly conserved Ca2+-binding site in a von Willebrand factor domain that may be central to Vg function, and the authors describe it as the first experimentally validated full-length Vg protein model. The EM map is low resolution and the Ca2+ site is predicted, not measured.

## Machine learning on plasma metabolites predicts acute kidney injury after cardiac surgery
2021-10-30 · medicine · Fuwai Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-10-plasma-metabolites-ml-csa-aki.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1161/jaha.121.021825

In 214 individuals (122 with acute kidney injury, 92 controls), untargeted and targeted metabolomics with several machine learning algorithms identified plasma metabolites associated with cardiac surgery-associated AKI; gluconic acid, fumaric acid and pseudouridine were upregulated. A random forest with clinical parameters and metabolites reached an AUC of 0.939 (95% CI 0.879-0.998), and the three metabolites rose over time in a swine AKI model. The abstract states a validation cohort confirmed the model, but its figure was truncated; the cohort is small.

Deep-learning image analysis quantified tissue damage in 789 kidney-transplant biopsy slides from two cohorts. A damage score from 12-month biopsies was associated with subsequent graft loss in both cohorts. ## Deep learning stroma-immune score predicts survival in stage II-III colorectal cancer
2021-10-30 · medicine · Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital; South China University of Technology
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-10-dl-stroma-immune-score-crc.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12935-021-02297-w

A convolutional neural network classified tissue on CD3 and CD8 immunohistochemistry whole-slide images, and a stroma-immune score was built from T-cell density in the stroma. Higher scores were associated with longer survival in development (N = 200), internal validation (N = 134) and external validation (N = 90) groups; in the development group, 5-year survival was 55.7% versus 80.8% for low versus high scores. ## Deep learning identifies skull fractures on cranial CT by detection and segmentation
2021-10-29 · medicine · Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Capital Medical University; Beijing Institute for Brain Disorders

YOLOv3 object detection and a modified attention U-Net segmentation network were developed on CT scans of 4,782 patients with skull fractures (development n = 4,168, test n = 614) plus 7,856 healthy people. On an external test set of 235 patients (93 with fracture) the attention U-Net had sensitivity 82.80% and specificity 88.73% versus 80.64% and 85.92% for YOLOv3. Labels came from neurologists at one source, sensitivity is moderate and there are no outcome data.

## EVE: evolutionary model predicts disease-variant pathogenicity without labels

EVE, an unsupervised deep generative model trained on evolutionary sequence variation across about 140,000 species, predicted pathogenicity for more than 36 million variants in 3,219 disease genes and classified over 256,000 variants of unknown significance. ## Machine learning prioritizes agonists for two human olfactory receptors
2021-10-26 · biology · Macquarie University; Duke University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-10-ml-human-olfactory-receptor-agonists.html
Source: https://www.mdpi.com/1422-0067/22/21/11546

A random-forest classifier trained from molecular descriptors screened five databases containing about 23 million compounds for agonists of human olfactory receptors OR1A1 and OR2W1. Following docking and researcher selection, the paper reports in-vitro activation by ethyl 2-(3-bromophenyl)acetate and methyl 2-(2-methylphenyl)acetate at OR1A1 and 2-ethoxynaphthalene at OR2W1. These are cell-assay results; they do not establish human perception, tissue safety or clinical benefit. The compounds were selected after multiple filters, so the results are not a database-wide hit rate. Prior ML work on related receptors exists; this record is limited to the reported candidates and assays.

## Real-time discovery and characterization of AT2020xnd, an AT2018cow-like fast transient
2021-10-09 · astronomy · Zwicky Transient Facility collaboration; California Institute of Technology; Liverpool John Moores University; University of California, Berkeley; collaborating observatories

ZTF observations identified AT2020xnd (ZTF20acigmel) at redshift 0.243 as the first unambiguous AT2018cow analogue found and confirmed in real time. Follow-up showed a rapid optical rise, persistently hot blue emission, luminous radio, millimetre and X-ray output, no classical radioactive-supernova peak, and a dwarf-galaxy host. ## SVM on serum metabolite profiles distinguishes oral squamous cell carcinoma
2021-09-27 · medicine · Nanjing University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-09-oscc-serum-metabolomics-svm.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.22541/au.163277427.72160941/v1

Serum from 819 volunteers (578 OSCC patients, 241 healthy controls) was profiled by conductive polymer spray ionization mass spectrometry. Univariate analysis selected 65 candidate metabolite ions, and DESI-MS imaging confirmed that 8 of the top 10 showed the same trends in tissue and serum. The design is case-control, the validation cohort size is not in the abstract, and univariate selection precedes the machine learning step.

A first-principles database and neural-network-potential search explored 396,862 Pt–Fe–Cu nanoparticle configurations and mapped candidate compositions. A generator–predictor–optimizer deep-learning workflow trained on quantitative delivery assays was used to design abiotic Mach miniproteins. Twelve selected predicted constructs were synthesized/tested; the strongest library construct improved phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PMO) delivery nearly 20-fold over unconjugated PMO in the standardized HeLa assay, while the authors describe the best designs as up to 50-fold more effective than prior polypeptide-based variants. PMO–Mach3/4 also produced dose-dependent reporter-protein restoration in skeletal muscle, diaphragm and heart in transgenic mice after a single intravenous dose.

DEEP2, trained on 3611 hours of colonoscopy video, was validated on 1393 hours from an unrelated source and reached 97.1% sensitivity at 4.6 false alarms per video; sensitivity was 88.5% and 84.9% for polyps visible under 5 and 2 seconds. ## Machine-learning unmixing links acid rain and subsurface flowpaths to watershed CO₂ drawdown
2021-06-17 · climate · Pennsylvania State University; Syracuse University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-06-machine-learning-unmixing-links-acid-rain-and-subsurface-flowpaths-to-watershed-co2-drawdown.html
Source: https://hess.copernicus.org/articles/25/3397/2021/index.html

Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) was applied to stream-chemistry time series from three watersheds to infer solute endmembers and their changing contributions without predefining endmember chemistry. Combined with geological interpretation and independent geochemical evidence, the model separated shallow acid-rain-affected flow from deeper pyrite-weathering contributions. The analysis found that acid rain can reduce a watershed’s long-timescale CO₂-sequestration capacity and that omitting sulfide oxidation/acid-rain reactions overestimates weathering-driven CO₂ drawdown.

## Machine learning identifies five synthesized Chevrel-phase tellurides with unusual channel-site occupancy
2021-06-09 · materials · University of California, Davis

## Satellite-image clustering guides discovery of four late Miocene fossil sites in Mozambique’s Urema Rift
2021-06-08 · biology · University of Oxford; University of Coimbra; University of North Carolina at Greensboro; University of Algarve; Gorongosa National Park
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-06-satellite-image-clustering-guides-discovery-of-four-late-miocene-fossil-sites-in-mozambiques-urema-rift.html
Source: https://peerj.com/articles/11573/

Unsupervised k-means clustering of seven Landsat 8 spectral bands highlighted a small set of priority areas for paleontological field survey in Gorongosa National Park. The 2018 campaign documented four new late Miocene fossil localities; three lay within the model’s target cluster and the fourth was less than 90 m away in the same gully system. Together, the sites expose the first reported estuarine coastal-forest fossil setting in the East African Rift System, filling a regional paleoenvironmental gap.

Across five independent transcriptomic datasets, the score tracked DAS28 disease activity, distinguished rheumatoid arthritis from osteoarthritis, separated polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis from healthy controls, and was associated with treatment effects. In an independent immunoblot cohort, two of six tested proteins, TNFAIP6/TSG-6 and HSP90AB1/HSP90, were confirmed.

Using explainable AI on single-forcing CESM1 large ensembles, the study identified the North Atlantic, Southern Ocean and Southeast Asia as key regional temperature patterns for dating the climate simulations, particularly before the early 21st century. ## Autonomous ML search and experiments find Fe–Co–Ir/Pt alloys above the Slater–Pauling magnetization limit

Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s43246-021-00135-0

A game-tree search using Gaussian-process predictions and first-principles calculations proposed dilute Ir and Pt additions as a counterintuitive way to raise Fe–Co magnetization. Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-02-random-forest-ctc-polyp-radiomics.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1148/radiol.2021202363

Polyps from a CT colonography screening trial were segmented and 1906 radiomic feature-filter combinations (shape, histogram, texture) were used to train a random forest on 107 polyps in 63 patients. In an external test set of 77 polyps in 59 patients it reached an AUC of 0.91 (95% CI 0.85 to 0.96), sensitivity 82% and specificity 85%, against a histopathology reference. The authors call it a proof-of-concept study with manual segmentation.

## Deep learning on chest X-ray detects elevated pulmonary artery wedge pressure
2021-02-18 · medicine · Tokushima University Hospital
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-02-cnn-chest-xray-elevated-wedge-pressure.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cjca.2021.02.007

Using 1013 consecutive patients with right-heart catheterization, a convolutional neural network was trained to identify elevated pulmonary arterial wedge pressure (above 18 mm Hg) from a chest X-ray. In the validation dataset, which the abstract calls prospective, the AUC was 0.77, similar to BNP (0.77) and an echocardiographic diastolic dysfunction algorithm (0.70) and higher than cardiothoracic ratio (0.66). ## Machine learning and ab initio screening predict 60 stable two-dimensional ferroelectric bimetal phosphates
2021-02-15 · materials · University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; and collaborators
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2021-02-machine-learning-and-ab-initio-screening-predict-60-stable-two-dimensional-ferroelectric-bimetal-phosphates.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.08527

A data-driven machine-learning search combined with high-throughput ab initio calculations screened 2,964 two-dimensional bimetal phosphates and identified 60 computationally stable structures with out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization: 16 predicted ferroelectric metals and 44 predicted ferroelectric semiconductors, including seven predicted multiferroics. In two independent cohorts (n=71 and n=32) AUROC was 0.74-0.78, similar to or better than FIB-4, APRI and NAFLD fibrosis score models.

A boosted regression tree model trained on pH from 18,386 wells predicted three-dimensional pH across the glacial aquifer system, with R2 0.60 on held-out data. A robotic electrochemistry stand coupled to Bayesian optimization tested 140 aqueous electrolyte formulas over 40 hours and selected a non-intuitive sodium mixture of NaClO4 and NaNO3. A graph neural network trained on a detailed N-body cosmological dark-matter simulation was distilled by symbolic regression into an analytic estimator for a halo’s overdensity from its mass and the masses, positions and velocities of nearby halos. On the analyzed simulation snapshot, the new expression reduced mean absolute error to 0.0882, compared with 0.121 for the authors’ existing hand-designed estimator. The formula’s mass-weighted neighborhood term decreases with separation and includes dependence on the central halo’s mass.

## AlphaFold wins CASP14 for protein folding

## DeepHL identified group-specific movement features in animal trajectories

DeepHL highlighted movement segments that distinguish animal groups. ## Hierarchical deep learning identifies corneal diseases from slit-lamp photographs
2020-10-20 · medicine · Department of Ophthalmology, The Affiliated Hospital of Guizhou Medical University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-10-corneal-disease-slit-lamp-deep-learning.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-020-75027-3

A hierarchical deep learning network was trained end-to-end on 5,325 retrospective ocular surface images and tested against 10 ophthalmologists in a prospective clinic-based dataset of 510 outpatients (infectious keratitis, non-infectious keratitis, corneal dystrophy or degeneration, corneal neoplasm). The area under the ROC curve was over 0.910 for each corneal disease type, with sensitivity and specificity similar to or better than the average of the ophthalmologists. The algorithm also outperformed four previously reported methods. The abstract describes it as possibly useful for computer-assisted diagnosis; clinical benefit was not tested.

## FermiNet: quantum physics of molecules from first principles
2020-10-19 · chemistry · Google DeepMind
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-10-ferminet.html
Source: https://deepmind.google/blog/ferminet-quantum-physics-and-chemistry-from-first-principles/

FermiNet approximates molecular ground-state electron wavefunctions from first principles. Against the coupled-cluster reference, it recovered 99.8% of the correlation energy beyond a single Slater determinant for the smallest molecules and at least 97% for bicyclobutane (30 electrons). It also modeled stretched nitrogen and hydrogen chains. These are computational results from the original work announced on 19 October 2020. The source page was updated on 22 August 2024 with a separate excited-state study; that later study's carbon-dimer error is not a 2020 result.

Analysis of high-resolution images located and measured the crowns of over 1.8 billion trees across 1.3 million km² of West Africa. Validation used manual annotations and field data; the study counts trees but does not yet measure their stored carbon.

The system plans multistep syntheses of complex natural products, with routes in a Turing-test study largely indistinguishable from human routes; three computer-designed syntheses were carried out in the lab: dauricine, tacamonidine, and lamellodysidine A. ## Akita: predicting 3D genome folding from DNA sequence

Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-020-0958-x

Akita, a convolutional network, predicts chromatin contact maps for about 1 Mb of DNA sequence. On held-out data it reaches a Pearson R of 0.61 and Spearman R of 0.56, and it learns an orientation-specific grammar for CTCF binding sites. ## Learned MRI brain-age gap associates with cognition and disability in geriatric depression

Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41398-020-01004-z

A pretrained convolutional brain-age estimator was applied without retuning to midlife and older-adult cohorts totaling 170 and 154 participants, respectively. Whole-exome data of 400 NSCLC patients from TCGA and an immune checkpoint cohort of 48 nivolumab-treated primary tumors were analyzed. A DeepLab v3 model trained on 110 metastasis-positive and 132 negative esophageal lymph node slides estimated metastasis probability on H&E slides. ## Deep learning on touchscreen typing screens fine-motor impairment in Parkinson's disease

Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-07-deep-learning-touchscreen-typing-parkinson.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-020-69369-1

Deep networks trained in initialization and fine-tuning stages estimated fine-motor impairment from smartphone typing. In a validation dataset of 36,000 typing sessions from 39 subjects (22 PD, 17 healthy) the AUC was 0.89, with 0.90 sensitivity and 0.83 specificity, and estimates correlated with UPDRS Part III items. An AUC of 0.97 was reported for 9 de novo patients versus 17 controls and 0.79 for 253 remote participants with self-reported health status.

## Machine learning estimates gestational age from newborn metabolic and clinical data
2020-07-25 · medicine · Ottawa Hospital Research Institute
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-07-gestational-age-metabolomics-elastic-net.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1101/2020.07.21.20158196

Elastic net regression models were derived from heel prick blood and clinical data of a retrospective Ontario newborn cohort and then applied to prospective birth cohorts in Zambia (N=311) and Bangladesh (N=1176). The best model estimated gestational age within about 6 days of early-pregnancy ultrasound for heel prick data (MAE 0.79 weeks in Zambia, 0.81 weeks in Bangladesh) and within about 7 days for cord blood data. Elastic net is penalized linear regression, a borderline machine learning method. Preprint of 2020-07-25.

Random-forest feature selection mapped plasma lipid profiles to triglyceride, HDL, LDL and total-cholesterol concentrations in plasma (n=777) and dried-blood-spot samples (n=835). ## Automated machine learning predicts screening-level PTSD in Danish soldiers

Automated machine learning applied to routine data from three cohorts of Danish soldiers (N = 232 to 352) predicted screening-level PTSD 2.5 and 6.5 years after deployment, with random forest AUC 0.77 and 0.78. ## Machine learning identifies seismic tremor precursors to Whakaari eruptions
2020-07-16 · physics · University of Auckland; University of Otago
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-07-machine-learning-identifies-seismic-tremor-precursors-to-whakaari-eruptions.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-17375-2

A structured machine-learning analysis of nine years of Whakaari seismic records identified four-hour energy bursts that occurred hours to days before most of the five major eruptive episodes studied. The authors interpret the pattern as possible charging of the vent hydrothermal system by hot magmatic fluids. In cross-validation, the prototype alert model gave advance warning for four of five unseen eruption instances, including at least four hours before the 2019 eruption.

Random-forest analysis of 4,323 Dutch home-care clients found that recorded nursing diagnoses and symptoms added information beyond existing case-mix groups. Genomes of 749 congenital heart disease probands and parents were compared with 1,611 unaffected trios. A deep learning method trained on in vitro loss-of-function screens predicted tumor-specific vulnerabilities in patient samples. It nominated Ran GTPase nucleocytoplasmic transport as a vulnerability in Her2-positive breast cancers and Ku70/80 for tumors defective in homologous recombination. ## Distinguishing vigilance decrement and low task demands from mind-wandering: A machine learning analysis of EEG.
2020-06-28 · multidisciplinary · Bernoulli Institute for Mathematics, Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence, University of Groningen, Groningen, The Netherlands
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-06-ejn-14863.html
Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7689771/

Across-task EEG classification found mind-wandering was separable from low vigilance and low task demand; the self-report-trained classifier predicted mind-wandering while classifiers trained on vigilance or task-demand labels did not, with source-localized features differing among states. Thirty participants; 10-fold and leave-one-participant-out cross-validation plus across-task testing against intermittent self-reports. Exploratory evidence with limited sample size and self-report labels.

## Elastic-net analysis links positive self-processing with reward motivation in depression

Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-06-study-10-1002-da-23042.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1002/da.23042

Elastic-net models compared cognitive and physiological predictors of self-reported reward responsivity and approach motivation in 202 young adults spanning depression severity. Positive self-referential processing was the most robust, modest predictor; held-out variance explained ranged from 5.0–12.2% for approach motivation and 9.7–28.0% for reward responsivity. Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/s2589-7500(20)30078-9

A CNN trained on contrast-enhanced CT from a Taiwanese centre reached 98.3% sensitivity on combined local test sets versus 92.9% for radiologists (difference 5.4 points, p=0.014). ## Neural MRI models classify liver tumors in a retrospective temporal validation cohort
2020-05-28 · medicine · Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital, Zhejiang University; Zhejiang University; Hwa Mei Hospital, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-05-liver-mri-clinical-neural-classification.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.3389/fonc.2020.00680

Inception-ResNet V2 networks were trained on MRI images from 1,210 patients to classify liver lesions, with evaluation in 201 later patients from the same hospital. Unenhanced MRI distinguished malignant from benign lesions with reported AUC 0.946; adding clinical data supported classification among malignant tumor types. The authors describe the later cohort as external, but their Methods identify a single-center temporal split. Malignancies required pathology, whereas some benign reference labels came from imaging reports. This supports retrospective diagnostic evaluation without establishing reduced contrast-agent harm, cost savings or benefit after clinical deployment.

## A learned twelve-gene signature stratifies lung-adenocarcinoma survival in archived cohorts

Source: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/oncology/articles/10.3389/fonc.2020.00835/full

Cox screening and random-survival-forest selection identified a twelve-gene immune-related score associated with overall survival in 954 lung-adenocarcinoma patients across four archived datasets. A 204-patient discovery cohort was followed by GEO validation cohorts totaling 309 patients and a 441-patient TCGA cohort; high-score groups had worse survival and distinct inferred immune profiles. Validation used a separate median cutoff in each cohort, and these retrospective associations do not demonstrate treatment-response prediction, clinical benefit or causal immune mechanisms.

## DeepMILO: a deep learning approach to predict the impact of non-coding sequence variants on 3D chromatin structure
2020-03-26 · medicine · Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-03-deepmilo-a-deep-learning-approach-to-predict-the-impact-of-non-coding.html
Source: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-020-01987-4

This method paper reports a specific cancer-genomics result (recurrent predicted loop disruption and association with BCL2/MYC expression), supported by learned sequence modeling and genomic expression analysis. Keep associations and predictions provisional. Methods/Results: CNN/RNN learn DNA sequence features for CTCF anchor/orientation and loop predictions. Test AUPRC varies by negative set (0.684 hardest); application to WGS of 1,834 patients across 12 cancer types predicts 672 insulator loops disrupted in ≥10% of patients; variants at anchors associated with BCL2/MYC upregulation in malignant lymphoma. ## Lung-CLiP machine learning detects early-stage lung cancer from cell-free DNA
2020-03-25 · medicine · Stanford University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-03-lung-clip-cfdna-lung-cancer-detection.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2140-0

Improved CAPP-Seq cfDNA analysis showed that ctDNA is present before treatment in most early-stage lung cancers and that most cfDNA mutations in patients and risk-matched controls reflect clonal haematopoiesis. Integrating these findings, the lung cancer likelihood in plasma (Lung-CLiP) machine-learning method discriminated early-stage patients from risk-matched controls with performance similar to tumour-informed ctDNA detection.

## EchoNet-Dynamic: video-based AI for left ventricular ejection fraction
2020-03-25 · medicine · Stanford University; Cedars-Sinai Medical Center
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-03-echonet-dynamic.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2145-8

A deep learning model trained on echocardiogram videos segmented the left ventricle with a Dice coefficient of 0.92 and estimated ejection fraction with a mean absolute error of 4.1% (6.0% on an external dataset from another health system). Prospective evaluation with repeated human measurements found its variance comparable to or lower than that of human experts. Caveat: training data come from one institution's echocardiograms, with external testing on a single additional system.

## Hospital audit study identifies limits of learned access explanations
2020-03-24 · computer science · University of Toronto; Mackenzie Richmond Hill Hospital
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-03-learned-hospital-access-audit-evaluation.html
Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32370950/

A hospital-field evaluation examined a machine-learning-based Explanation-Based Auditing System using staff access logs and scenario checks. The tool explained an average98.09% of accesses as appropriate; this measures explanation coverage, rather than breach-detection accuracy. Analysis linked many unexplained accesses to missing staff metadata and exceptional workflows, identifying limits that remained despite high overall coverage. This single-hospital evaluation does not establish fewer privacy breaches or generalizable detection performance.

## Longitudinal records supported forecasts of multiple sclerosis progression

Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-03-ms-course-ml.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0230219

The study used routine records from 1,624 people with multiple sclerosis to forecast transition from relapsing-remitting to secondary-progressive disease at 180, 360 and 720 days. Visit-based models had 70–100% recall but 5–10% precision without confidence filtering; the history model reached 67% recall and 42% precision at 720 days. ## CNNs predict age and sex from fundus images in hypertension, diabetes and smoking
2020-03-12 · medicine · Seoul National University; Seoul National University Bundang Hospital; Kangdong Sacred Heart Hospital
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-03-cnn-fundus-age-sex-vascular-conditions.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-020-61519-9

CNN models trained on 219,302 fundus images of healthy participants predicted age with R2 0.92 and mean absolute error 3.06 years in normal test images. Errors were similar in hypertension (3.46 years), diabetes (3.55) and smokers (2.65), but R2 was lower (0.74, 0.75 and 0.86), and sex prediction had AUC above 0.96. The authors interpret this as ageing and vascular changes having different retinal features; the data come from one archive, so this is suggestive.

## Combining AI algorithms with radiologists improves mammography specificity
2020-03-02 · medicine · Sage Bionetworks; and DREAM challenge collaborators, with US and Swedish screening programmes
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-03-mammography-ai-challenge-radiologists.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2020.0265

An international crowdsourced challenge (over 1,100 participants, 126 teams, 44 countries) tested AI on screening mammograms from 144,231 US and 166,578 Swedish examinations. The best single algorithm did not beat radiologists (US AUC 0.858), but an ensemble of top algorithms combined with US radiologists' recall decisions reached AUC 0.942 and 92.0% specificity at the same sensitivity. The study is retrospective, uses challenge data and does not report recall rates.

Machine-learning algorithms and deep neural networks were trained on electronic health records to produce a calibrated risk score for suicide attempt in the following year. ## Machine learning identifies IgA nephropathy subgroups that benefit from immunosuppression

Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ebiom.2020.102657

Using clinical and pathological data from 4047 biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy patients at 24 Chinese centres (derivation 2058, validation 1989), model-based recursive partitioning found three subgroups with long-term immunosuppression benefit for kidney failure. Examples are creatinine at most 1.437 mg/dl with proteinuria above 2.480 g/24h (HR 0.23) and, at higher creatinine, high proteinuria with crescents (HR 0.29). Support vector regression on CSF, MRI, amyloid-PET and FDG-PET biomarkers was trained in autosomal-dominant Alzheimer's disease (n = 121) and cross-validated in sporadic prodromal AD (n = 216). Source: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2019.03000/full

MALDI-TOF spectra from 33 C. albicans isolates from 15 patients were analyzed using 32 ML algorithms across six preparation conditions; an LDA pipeline reached 85.71% accuracy, 83.33% sensitivity and 88.89% specificity. Evidence is limited to the stated retrospective/in-silico/prototype setting. External replication and prospective utility were not established in the reviewed material.

## A LASSO-selected snoRNA signature stratifies head-neck cancer survival
2020-01-14 · medicine · Shandong University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-01-study-10-1002-jcp-29462.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1002/jcp.29462

A LASSO-Cox pipeline selected a five-snoRNA expression signature from TCGA head-and-neck cancer data. A 357-patient training set and 153-patient internal test set supported retrospective survival stratification. Functional interpretations came from coexpression and enrichment rather than perturbation experiments. The signature requires external validation and does not establish clinical benefit or a causal role for the RNAs.

## Supervised machine learning gives an MRI atrophy-pattern score for Alzheimer's disease
2020-01-14 · medicine · University Medicine Greifswald
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-01-alzheimer-atrophy-pattern-ai-score.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyt.2019.00953

A supervised model trained on ADNI-1 MRI scans assigned a continuous AD score from regional atrophy patterns. It separated patients from controls with accuracy 89% (AUC 0.95) in ADNI-1 and 87% (AUC 0.93) in the independent OASIS-1 sample, and the score was associated with MMSE and weakly with verbal memory in a population sample (SHIP-Trend). The data are retrospective public cohorts.

## Deep learning, computer-aided radiography reading for tuberculosis: a diagnostic accuracy study from a tertiary hospital in India
2020-01-14 · medicine · Department of Epidemiology, Biostatistics and Occupational Health, McGill University, Montreal, Canada; McGill International TB Centre, McGill University, Montreal, Canada; Department of Radiodiagnosis, Kasturba Medical College, Manipal, Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Manipal, India; Department of Medicine, Kasturba Medical College, Manipal, Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Manipal, India; Department of Microbiology, Kasturba Medical College, Manipal, Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Manipal, India; Manipal McGill Program for Infectious Diseases, Manipal Centre for Infectious Diseases, Prasanna School of Public Health, Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Manipal, India; Department of Infectious Diseases, Kasturba Medical College, Manipal, Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Manipal, India
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-01-1038-s41598-019-56589-3.html
Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-019-56589-3.pdf

Against microbiological confirmation, qXR reached AUC 0.81, 71% sensitivity and 80% specificity; radiologist sensitivity was 56% with 80% specificity. Retrospective case-control cohort of 317 confirmed cases and 612 controls at one tertiary hospital; specificity/sensitivity limits and need for prospective studies are stated by the authors.

## Machine-learning-selected variables give parsimonious classifiers for ARDS phenotypes
2020-01-13 · medicine · University of California, San Francisco
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-01-parsimonious-ards-phenotype-classifiers.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/s2213-2600(19)30369-8

Random forest, bagging and LASSO selected important variables from three ARDS Network trial cohorts (n=2022), which fed nested logistic regression classifiers of the hyperinflammatory and hypoinflammatory phenotypes. Three-variable (IL-8, bicarbonate, protein C) and four-variable models reached AUC 0.94 and 0.95 in the validation set SAILS (n=715) against latent class analysis labels. The hyperinflammatory phenotype had higher day-90 mortality (39% vs 23%) in the validation set; this is a retrospective secondary analysis with latent-class labels as the reference.

## Machine learning predicts gestational diabetes from nationwide electronic health records
2020-01-13 · medicine · Weizmann Institute of Science
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-01-ml-gestational-diabetes-ehr-prediction.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-019-0724-8

Models trained on retrospective records of 588,622 pregnancies in Israel predicted gestational diabetes at pregnancy initiation with an auROC of 0.85 against 0.68 for a baseline risk score. Results held on a future validation set and a geographical validation set from Jerusalem, and a nine-question model reached an auROC of 0.80.

## Detecting Suspected Pump Thrombosis in Left Ventricular Assist Devices via Acoustic Analysis.
2020-01-13 · medicine · School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, USA
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-01-detecting-suspected-pump-thrombosis-in-left-ventricular-assist-devices-via-acousti.html
Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7380556/

Among 13 HVAD recipients, reported accuracy was 88.9% and sensitivity 90.9%; post-thrombolysis recordings suggested abnormalities not identified by reference pump-power or biomarker measures. The small suspected-thrombosis series and post-treatment observations are not independent prospective validation or proof of clinical benefit.

## deepDTnet repurposes topotecan as an RORγt inhibitor for multiple-sclerosis models
2020-01-13 · medicine · Cleveland Clinic; Case Western Reserve University, Harvard Medical School and collaborators
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-01-deepdtnet-repurposes-topotecan-as-an-rort-inhibitor-for-multiple-sclerosis-models.html
Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34123272/

The deep-learning network deepDTnet predicted retinoic-acid-receptor-related orphan receptor gamma-t (RORγt) as a previously unrecognized target of topotecan. Biochemical assays showed direct inhibition (IC50 0.43 μM), and topotecan improved outcomes in a mouse experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis model of multiple sclerosis.

## Combination of a Big Data Analytics Resource System With an Artificial Intelligence Algorithm to Identify Clinically Actionable Radiation Dose Thresholds for Dysphagia in Head and Neck Patients.
2020-01-12 · medicine · Department of Radiation Oncology, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, Michigan

Source: https://europepmc.org/article/MED/33305091

The full article reports an exploratory learned-ranking analysis of 132 head-and-neck radiotherapy patients, relating dose-volume measures to grade ≥2 dysphagia; specific dose thresholds are proposed from this selected cohort. These are exploratory associations and not independent or causal validation.

## Unraveling the molecular heterogeneity in type 2 diabetes: a potential subtype discovery followed by metabolic modeling
2020-01-09 · medicine · Laboratory of Complex Biological Systems and Bioinformatics (CBB), Department of Bioinformatics, Institute of Biochemistry and Biophysics (IBB), University of Tehran, Tehran, Iran
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-01-unraveling-the-molecular-heterogeneity-in-type-2-diabetes-a-potential-subtype-disc.html

Primary BMC Medical Genomics Results identify three T2DM expression clusters and distinct metabolic flux/gene patterns from 154 skeletal-muscle profiles; the earlier Research Square V1 reports the same three clusters and pathway result. ## Deep neural networks diagnose brain tumours in minutes from stimulated Raman histology
2020-01-06 · medicine · University of Michigan; Columbia University; University of Miami
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-01-stimulated-raman-brain-tumor-diagnosis.html
Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-019-0715-9

CNNs trained on over 2.5 million stimulated Raman histology images produced intraoperative brain tumour diagnoses in under 150 seconds, with 94.6% accuracy versus 93.9% for pathologists. The accuracy comparison comes from a prospective multicentre trial with 278 patients, but the abstract does not report sensitivity or specificity separately.

## An AI breast-cancer screening system evaluated in two countries
2020-01-01 · medicine · Google DeepMind; Google Health, Cancer Research UK Imperial Centre, and Northwestern University
Page: https://aisciencetracker.org/share/2020-01-screening-seno.html
Source: https://deepmind.google/blog/international-evaluation-of-an-ai-system-for-breast-cancer-screening/

Among 25,856 women in the UK and 3,097 in the US, the system reduced false positives by 5.7% (US) and 1.2% (UK), and false negatives by 9.4% and 2.7% in absolute terms compared with radiologists. Trained only on UK data, it also outperformed specialists on US data. Retrospective evaluation (Nature): prospective studies are needed, and clinical deployment is unclear.
